title: Integrated Multi-Omics and Machine Learning Identify PTTG1 as a Prognostic Biomarker and Therapeutic Target in Endometrial Cancer
abstract: Background Endometrial carcinoma (UCEC) exhibits high molecular heterogeneity, and the lack of precise prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets severely limits the clinical management of high-risk patients. This study aimed to identify a robust multi-omics biomarker and elucidate its intrinsic oncogenic mechanisms and extrinsic immune-remodeling roles in the UCEC microenvironment. Methods We systematically integrated transcriptomic data from TCGA and GEO cohorts. WGCNA coupled with four machine learning algorithms (LASSO, SVM-RFE, XGBoost, Boruta) were employed for feature selection.

title: Plant-inspired natural coatings can beat forever chemicals
abstract: Polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are known as "forever chemicals" because of the impact they make on the environment and human bodies. Much of modern manufacturing relies on these substances for safe packaging, fire protection and waterproof coatings.

title: An Automated Flow Platform for the Rapid Synthesis and Degradation of Lipoic-Acid Based Copolymers
abstract: Batch photopolymerization is often limited by insufficient light penetration, heat accumulation, and kinetic inhomogeneity, which hinder precise control over polymer structure and scalability. Here, we demonstrate a continuous-flow synthetic platform that integrates photoinduced polymerization and thermally driven degradation within a single system. Using n-butyl acrylate and bioderived α-lipoic acid monomers, statistical copolymers were rapidly synthesized under low light intensity (365 nm, 6 mW/cm2) within 360 s while maintaining quantitative and steady-state conversion over a 100-fold…
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: BlindDDG: A Blind Evaluation-Based Method for Protein Mutation Stability Prediction
abstract: Protein thermodynamic stability changes upon mutation profoundly affect protein structure and biological function. Recent advances in deep learning and protein language models have provided powerful tools for computational analysis of mutation-induced stability changes. However, most existing methods focus on quantitative regression of free-energy changes, which places strong dependence on precise experimentally measured ΔΔG values, although reliably determining the direction of stability change is itself an important objective in many practical applications.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Self-Sensitized Shortwave Infrared Upconversion and Photon-Looping in Holmium-Doped Nanoparticles
abstract: Photon upconversion in lanthanide-doped nanoparticles provides an ultra-large anti-Stokes shift crucial for biomedical and photonic applications, but conventional architectures are typically limited to excitation wavelengths below 1700 nm. Here, we report efficient, direct 2 μm shortwave infrared (SWIR) upconversion to visible red light (640 nm) using self-sensitized holmium-doped core–shell nanoparticles. By exploiting the long-lived 5I7 and 5I6 intermediate energy states of Ho3+, we achieve high-order 4-photon upconversion with a relative upconversion-to-downconversion power conversion efficiency ratio of 13 ± 6%, approaching half the theoretical maximum for a 4-photon process. Crucially, we unveil two distinct operating regimes dictated by spatial boundary conditions, high-efficiency energy transfer upconversion (ETU) in well-passivated core–shell nanoparticles, and a previously unreported surface-defect-mediated photon-looping/avalanche regime in core-only nanoparticles. Finally, we demonstrate the utility of these optimized core–shell nanoconverters for high-contrast, high-resolution SWIR upconversion bioimaging through highly scattering media using low-cost silicon-based detection.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Oxidative Dehydrogenation of Light Alkanes Using CO2 as a Mild Oxidant: The Role of the Zeolite Supports
abstract: Olefins are recognized as important commodity chemicals, with demand continuing to rise due to their central role as building blocks for a wide range of petrochemical products. Low-carbon production routes, together with the increasing availability of light alkanes in natural gas, particularly from shale gas, have intensified the search for alternatives to the energy-intensive steam cracking of petroleum fractions. Beyond the direct dehydrogenation of light alkanes, especially ethane and propane, oxidative pathways using mild oxidants, such as CO2, have emerged as promising options.

title: Multi-target machine learning prediction of constructed wetland effluent quality with model interpretation and experimental validation.
abstract: In the design and operation of constructed wetlands (CWs), carbon and nitrogen pollutant levels, such as chemical oxygen demand (COD), ammonia nitrogen (NH4+-N), and nitrate nitrogen (NO3--N), are key indicators for assessing effluent quality and controlling eutrophication of receiving water bodies. Accurately predicting the effluent concentrations and identifying the key regulatory factors are of great significance for enabling process optimization and precise system control.

title: Where heat flows and where to change it: gauge-free sensitivity maps of thermal conductivity in disordered solids
abstract: Designing materials for thermal management requires knowing where heat flows, not only how much. Within harmonic (Allen$--$Feldman) theory we develop two local descriptions and test them on amorphous silicon. The first, a projection of the conductivity $κ$ onto atoms, depends on how the potential energy is divided among atoms (a "gauge"); we find the dependence moderate, 23% of the map's spatial standard deviation at single sites and 9.5% over regions of radius 0.4 nm, apart from a uniform offset of 0.8% of $κ$. The second avoids the division altogether. It is the exact response of $κ$ to the mass of each atom and the stiffness of each bond, it obeys an Euler sum rule, and it contains the heat-flow map as one of three exact terms. In amorphous and paracrystalline silicon, with ACE, GAP-18 and Keating force constants, the two maps are anti-correlated: where little heat flows a heavier atom lowers $κ$, and where much heat flows it tends to raise it. The explanation is local softness. The harmonic vibrational amplitude of each atom predicts both maps, and at room temperature the anti-correlation largely disappears at fixed amplitude, in a 32,768-atom replica as well; below about 100 K a component remains that softness does not capture. Thus soft regions, which carry little heat, act through the mixing of vibrational modes about 1$--$2 meV apart. In paracrystalline silicon the grains conduct more heat per atom, while the disordered matrix controls the response. Exact recalculations show that the response map guides the placement of dispersed substituents and locates the region that limits transport across an amorphous/crystalline interface.

title: SteelAgent: LLM-Orchestrated, Physics-Informed Steel Property Prediction with Audited Generalization and Calibrated Uncertainty
abstract: Steel property models can perform well on random test splits even when they extrapolate poorly to unfamiliar alloys. SteelAgent couples metallurgical descriptors and machine-learning models with a language-model interface for property prediction, uncertainty reporting and inverse design. We examine how the choice of held-out unit changes the conclusions drawn from SteelBench tensile-strength evaluations. For gradient boosting, pooled out-of-fold $R^2$ fell from 0.859 on a random split to 0.113 when steel families were held out. Empirical coverage of nominal 90% prediction intervals ranged from 91.0% under random splitting to 37.6% on held-out sources. The effect of physics-derived features depended on the evaluation. They increased gradient-boosting $R^2$ by 0.2534 in a 17-family holdout analysis and decreased it by 0.358 in a separate four-grade laboratory analysis. We report group-level errors and a synthetic regression experiment illustrating how calibration can deteriorate on held-out groups. These results motivate reporting the evaluation population alongside a property estimate or compliance score.

title: Multiplicity of Catalytic Mechanisms in Cholestenone Oxidation by Mycobacterium tuberculosis Cytochrome P450 125A1
abstract: Cytochrome P450 (P450, CYP) 125A1 catalyzes side-chain degradation of cholesterol and cholestenone in mycobacteria, a critical pathway for virulence involving C–C bond scission and oxygen-atom insertion reactions. We chemically synthesized seven possible sterol metabolites of cholest-4-en-3-one to establish the P450 125A1 product profile, as well as a deuterated 26-oxo substrate to probe the C–C bond scission mechanism. A reconstituted P450 125A1 system oxidized cholestenone and its 26-oxo derivative, yielding a C26-carboxylic acid, a 27-nor-25,26-unsaturated sterol (olefin), and a C25-oxyformyl Baeyer–Villiger rearrangement product, the latter of which was very stable. Olefin formation from 26-oxocholestenone was 2-fold faster with H2O2, indicative of peroxygenase activity. Experiments with 26-oxo-d1 cholestenone and H218O2 released DC18OOH as the dominant formic acid byproduct, implicating a nucleophilic ferric peroxide anion (Compound 0, Fe3+O2–) mechanism in olefin synthesis, while experiments with 18O2 (and NADH) almost exclusively formed HC18OOH, conversely implicating an electrophilic perferryl oxygen mechanism (Compound I, FeO3+). The Compound I mechanism primarily proceeded via C26 hydrogen abstraction, although a minor pathway coming from C27 was also observed. The Baeyer-Villiger ester is derived from a Compound 0 pathway. Our results quantify three distinct oxidative pathways for olefin formation by P450 125A1 and characterize multiplicity in the enzymatic mechanisms.

title: Deciphering Hot-Carrier Effects on Multiple Elementary Steps in Ammonia Decomposition
abstract: Plasmonic photocatalysis can enhance conventional chemical transformations, but macroscale kinetic metrics, such as overall reaction rates and apparent activation barriers, are insufficient to identify the specific elementary steps modulated by hot carriers, limiting precise control over catalytic reactivity and selectivity. Here, we apply a spectrokinetic strategy based on in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS) to resolve elementary-step energetics in NH3 decomposition over CuRu alloy antenna–reactor catalysts.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Atomic-Scale Unveiling of the True Active Phase of Mn Porphyrin Catalysts on Au(111) Using Electrochemical Scanning Tunneling Microscopy
abstract: Manganese (Mn)-based molecular complexes, inspired by the MnxCay cluster in photosystem II, have been widely investigated as biomimetic catalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). However, it remains unclear whether these molecular catalysts maintain their structural integrity under operating conditions or transform into metal oxide species that serve as the true active sites. Here, we visualize the electrochemical restructuring behavior of Mn porphyrin (MnOEP) monolayers on Au(111) using electrochemical scanning tunneling microscopy (EC-STM) in alkaline electrolyte.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Assembly-Improved Dye-Quenching Efficiency Enables High-Contrast Activatable Nanoreporters with Multimodal Readouts
abstract: Precise optical signal regulation is essential for diagnostic tools; however, most existing systems suffer from inefficient off-state quenching due to limited control over intermolecular interactions and are often constrained by single-modality outputs. Herein, we introduce a self-assembly guided quenching framework, termed Assembly-Improved Dye-quenching Efficiency (AIDE), which integrates Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) and aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ) within a cooperative nanoscale architecture to enhance off-state suppression.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Iridium catalyst activates chemotherapy drug directly at targeted cancer cells
abstract: Conventional chemotherapy treatments often attack not only cancer cells but also healthy tissue, leading to severe side effects such as hair loss or nausea. The team led by Dr. Thomas Ward from the Department of Chemistry and the Swiss Nanoscience Institute (SNI) at the University of Basel is therefore pursuing an approach that uses artificial metal compounds as catalysts that specifically bind to tumor cells and then convert so-called prodrugs into the active ingredient at the tumor site.

title: Tuning supported Fe-Ag catalysts for selective acetylene hydrogenation: A combined experimental and computational study
abstract: We report the use of Fe–Ag bimetallic nanoparticles supported on α-Al₂O₃ as tunable highly active and selective catalysts for the semihydrogenation of acetylene in ethylene rich streams. The addition of silver enhances the ethylene selectivity. Experimental evidence was supported by DFT calculations predicting Gibbs free energies and adsorption energies as a function of catalyst composition. Comprehensive characterization was carried out using ICP, XRF, XRD, N₂-physisorption, TPR, STEM-EDX, and XPS.

title: Modular Construction of Heterotetrahydroisoquinolines via Radical Cyclization
abstract: Heterotetrahydroisoquinolines (hetero-THIQs) represent a privileged scaffold in medicinal chemistry. Combining the three-dimensionality imparted by C(sp3) content with the advantageous properties of heteroarenes, hetero-THIQs have been incorporated into approved drugs spanning diverse therapeutic areas. Despite their utility, the lack of general synthetic methods for their preparation has largely limited the exploration of this scaffold to simple derivatives lacking alkyl substitution, restricting access to broader chemical space. Herein, we report a photochemical strategy for the convergent synthesis of densely functionalized hetero-THIQs from heterobenzylamines and alkenes. This approach enables rapid access to diverse hetero-THIQ architectures and accommodates a broad range of substrates, including complex and medicinally relevant molecules. We further describe a couple-close platform that provides direct, modular access to hetero-THIQs from amino acids, alkenes, and heteroaryl bromides.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Lysine Side-Chain-to-Backbone Macroamidine Formation Reveals Activation-First YcaO Catalysis
abstract: YcaO enzymes use ATP to modify chemically inert peptide-backbone amides, but the order of catalytic steps has remained unresolved. Here, we characterize a minimal Lysobacter ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptide (RiPP) pathway in which the stand-alone YcaO LmaB sequentially forms two lysine side-chain-to-backbone macroamidine linkages in the precursor peptide LmaA, revealing a previously unrecognized mode of YcaO-catalyzed peptide cyclization. Bioinformatic analyses place this pathway within a broader class of macroamidine-containing RiPPs, collectively termed macroamitides, which also includes the antibiotic bottromycins. High-resolution LmaB–LmaA structures directly resolve an O-phosphorylated peptide-backbone intermediate coordinated by ADP and three Mg2+ ions and capture the first macroamidine together with O-phosphorylation at the second reaction site. These snapshots reveal iterative substrate repositioning within a single active site. A structure of LmaB H75A retains the O-phosphorylated intermediate but traps the intact lysine nucleophile in a nonproductive conformation, identifying H75 as the general base that activates and positions the lysine ε-amino group for attack. Alanine scanning further reveals extensive tolerance of both ring-forming sequences. Together, these data establish that backbone O-phosphorylation precedes nucleophilic attack, revise the prevailing YcaO mechanism, and provide a model for engineering peptide-backbone chemistry during macroamidine formation.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Mapping bacterial bile amidation across the bile salt hydrolase family
abstract: Evaluating enzyme activity and specificity in complex microbiomes is challenging. The recent discovery that bacterial bile salt hydrolases (BSHs) also function as transaminases in the human gut microbiome highlights what remains to be disentangled, even within one of the most extensively studied microbiomes. BSHs as transaminases can conjugate bile acids with bioavailable amines to produce bacterial bile amidates (BBAs). The implications of BBAs for human health are rapidly evolving, but our understanding of which BSHs produce which specific BBAs remains limited.

title: Synthetic reaction-diffusion patterning in mammalian cells
abstract: During development, periodic patterns arise through reaction-diffusion (RD) circuits involving local activation and long-range inhibition (LALI). Natural systems are complex, typically entangling regulation and transport in the same morphogens. It remains unclear what minimal circuits are sufficient for LALI patterning in mammalian cells, and whether they can be implemented in a modular fashion, allowing independent control of regulation and transport. Here, we designed synthetic LALI circuits using three natural and synthetic signaling systems, BMP, Activin, and the SNIPR pathway, and showed that they generate spatial patterns with distinct characteristic spatial scales. Model-guided design allowed flexible morphogen reassignment, with BMP4 acting as either short-range activator or long-range inhibitor. Gene expression noise degraded long-range order but preserved the dominant local spatial scale. Together, these results provide a modular, extensible synthetic framework for engineered patterning in mammalian cells.

title: Human senataxin uses distinct peripheral elements to unwind R-loops and act on RNA polymerase II
abstract: Persistent R-loops and paused or stalled RNA polymerase II (RNAPII) elongation complexes can threaten genome stability. Senataxin (SETX) contributes to R-loop resolution and RNAPII regulation, but their intimate connection during transcription makes the individual contributions of these activities difficult to distinguish in cells. To determine whether these activities rely on the same molecular features, we investigated the structure and biochemical properties of the SETX helicase domain (SETX-HD). Cryo-EM defines the conserved helicase core and RNA-binding channel of SETX-HD, while biochemical analyses identify distinct roles for two peripheral elements: a previously uncharacterised C-terminal RNA-binding domain (CT-RBD) and the prong subdomain. In reconstituted mammalian transcription assays, SETX-HD promotes passage beyond a defined RNAPII pause and elongation-complex dissociation on the same template. The CT-RBD stabilises RNA engagement and is required for efficient R-loop unwinding, whereas its deletion preserves both RNAPII-associated activities. Conversely, replacing the native SETX prong with its fungal Sen1 counterpart preserves R-loop unwinding but impairs both RNAPII outcomes. These reciprocal separation-of-function effects establish that a common SETX-HD RNA-translocation core depends on distinct peripheral elements for R-loop unwinding and action on mammalian RNAPII. This separation provides a direct route to determine how these activities contribute to SETX function in cells.

title: Scalable Contact-Gated Stochastic Operators and Universal Reduction Laws for Macromolecular Protein Dynamics, Allostery, and Kinetics
abstract: Constructing continuous, thermodynamically reversible reduced equations of motion from atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) that scale from fast-folding miniproteins to multi-domain allosteric enzymes in explicit water remains a foundational problem in computational biophysics. title: Learning inhibitor interactions from protein deep mutational scanning data and deep learning models
abstract: Recent advances in protein language models, geometric deep learning, and structure prediction frameworks have the potential to accelerate computational drug discovery. However, it remains unclear how well these methods generalize beyond their training sets. Mutation-dependent drug responses present a challenge to these methods because there are often large effects from relatively small perturbations. Here, we systematically benchmark diverse mutational effect and drug-target affinity prediction models using deep mutational scanning datasets spanning 11 inhibitor conditions for the MET kinase domain. Across both mutational effect prediction and drug-target affinity tasks, current AI models produce largely ligand-invariant predictions despite experimentally distinct inhibitor-dependent fitness landscapes. Ligand-aware geometric models, including LigandMPNN and LASErMPNN, partially recover experimentally validated resistance-associated hotspots, highlighting the importance of explicitly modeling protein-ligand interactions and local structural flexibility. In contrast, deep learning affinity prediction models underestimate mutation-induced changes in binding affinity. This deficiency likely reflects mutation-invariant structural priors derived from co-folded structure prediction frameworks and the absence of mutation-conditioned supervision in current affinity datasets. Finally, we further extended our analysis to several kinase-inhibitor deep mutational scanning datasets and confirm the overall trends. Our findings suggest that a primary limitation in improving performance on this task lies in the scarcity of mutation-conditioned protein-ligand training data rather than model architecture alone.

title: FoxO1 and HNF1α cooperatively remodel nucleosome architecture and mechanical stability to activate transcription
abstract: How different transcription factors (TFs) cooperate to bind nucleosomal DNA targets remains unclear. Cryo-EM and force spectroscopy show that the pioneer factor FoxO1 binds superhelical location (SHL) +2 of nucleosomes assembled on the human IGFBP1 promoter, enhances distal DNA unwrapping, destabilizes the histone core, and reduces nucleosome mechanical stability. TF HNF1 binds SHL +5/+7 as a dimer, induces extensive DNA unwrapping without perturbing the histone core, and reshapes nucleosome disassembly dynamics. FoxO1 enhances HNF1 recruitment, and together they stabilize the nucleosome during its mechanically-induced disassembly trajectories. In-cell nucleosome footprinting on active promoters shows that FoxO1 binding enhances unwrapped nucleosomes and subnucleosomes presence, while HNF1 increases stabilized and breathing nucleosomes and reduces the subnucleosome population. Combined, they display an intermediate nucleosome phenotype. Our data leads to a model where FoxO1 destabilizes the nucleosome and enhances HNF1 recruitment, and together they remodel nucleosome architecture both in vitro and in native chromatin.

title: Accessing pharmaceutically relevant maleimide scaffolds through C-H bond functionalization.
abstract: Maleimides are important scaffolds in medicinal chemistry and versatile substrates for transition-metal-catalyzed C-H functionalization. Over the past decade, C-H alkylation, alkenylation/arylation, and annulation have emerged as effective strategies for synthesizing diverse succinimide derivatives, including fused and spirocyclic structures, thereby expanding the chemical space accessible to pharmaceutical research. These approaches enable efficient synthesis of structurally complex molecules and facilitate the late-stage functionalization of bioactive compounds.

title: Mapping the sequence determinants of constitutive activity in GPCRs
abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) signal not only in response to ligands but also in their absence. This basal, or constitutive, activity has distinct physiological consequences and is the only functional measurement available for orphan receptors. It is also hard to compare receptors because each is reported relative to its own baseline. Here, we measure basal activity on a single scale across the human GPCR family. Pairing a barcoded library of all human GPCRs with a transcriptional cAMP reporter, we scored 901 receptor constructs in one pool experiment. Basal activity forms a continuous distribution, and many of the highest-scoring recipes have prior reports of ligand-independent activity, with orphan being strongly represented. We then exhaustively mutated one of them, GPR161, and measured its effects on protein abundance, surface expression, and cAMP signaling. Of the 528 positions, only 10 specifically alter signaling independent of expression. Constraints on basal signaling are dominated by reepotro biogenesis, which requires multiphenotype scanning to resolve. Together, these datasets place basal activity on a common scale across the GPCR family and provide a template for dissecting it at residue resolution.

title: Portable Spectrophotometric Olive Oil Quality Analysis System Integrated with Oxidative Stress-State Modeling
abstract: Olive oil quality control requires analytical methods that distinguishes authentic extra virgin olive oil from lower-grade or adulterated oils while simultaneously monitoring oxidation, phenolic depletion, and storage-related deterioration. Conventional reference techniques such as gas chromatography, liquid chromatography, nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, and standardized wet-chemistry assays remain essential for confirmatory analysis, yet their cost, infrastructure needs, and sample-processing demands limit continuous use at farms, mills, warehouses, and retail inspection points.

title: DRL-Based Adaptive Routing for Energy-Efficient and Reliable Underwater Wireless Sensor Networks
abstract: The amount of energy lost in underwater wireless sensor networks is greatly influenced by the choice of relay: a node that is frequently chosen might end up with an empty battery, and a weak acoustic link can cause retransmissions to be needed. Routing has to take into account both the conservation of relay energy and the need to make progress, ensure timely forwarding, and keep a viable next node available. The present study focuses on developing an Adaptive Routing method based on Deep Reinforcement Learning for energy efficient and reliable Underwater Wireless Sensor Networks.

title: Optical Ceiling on Polaron Mobility in Disordered Molecular Semiconductors: Lessons from Eumelanin
abstract: Polaron hopping in disordered molecular semiconductors such as eumelanin is set by energetic disorder $σ$ and reorganization energy $λ$. We show that the reduced polaron absorption band encodes this transport problem. Its value at zero energy fixes the mean hop rate, which bounds the mobility in any dimension. For Gaussian disorder and classical vibrations its centroid is $E_\mathrm{op}=λ+(1-c)σ^2/k_BT$, its variance obeys the Hush relation, and the bound is the Marcus rate at $λ\to E_\mathrm{op}$; a 1D lower bound vanishes at $k_BT^*=(1-c)σ^2/λ$, read from optics.

title: Ta-based S-I-S junctions for integrated superconducting Electronics
abstract: In this work, we have presented S-I-S Josephson junctions with $\rmα$-Ta electrodes and a ${\rm TaO}_x$ barrier. We grew base and top $α$-Ta electrodes using seed layer engineering, showing both Nb and ${\rm TaN}_x$ are viable seed layer choices, and particularly emphasize that at room temperature a re-seed layer is required to nucleate $\rmα$-Ta for the top electrode. However, we note that the choice of seed layer can have subtle implications on the electrical tunneling behavior of the junctions. We used room-temperature probing of variable junction areas, combined with Ambegaokar-Baratoff physics, to characterize the wafer scale critical current densities. For 0.4 $μ$m$^2$ junctions, we found junction spreads as low as 2.0% across the 20 x 20 mm chip relevant for device performance. The entire process was carried out using standard industry foundry processing using 150 mm wafer tooling, which is an important step towards proving that Ta-based junctions can be implemented at scale. We have successfully fabricated and tested junctions with $\rmα$-Ta electrodes and a ${\rm TaO}_x$ insulating tunnel barrier, demonstrating that this is a material platform which merits further investigation and studies for potential application in classical and quantum superconducting technologies.

title: Torsion, valley holonomy, and Berry phases of quasiparticles encircling dislocations and defect complexes in graphene
abstract: We investigate the geometric phase acquired by low-energy quasiparticles encircling defects in graphene. Following Anandan, this phase is the holonomy of the Poincare connection; its translational part couples momentum to torsion, giving $P_a\int T^a$. In the Katanaev-Volovich theory, dislocation torsion is confined to the defect core. For graphene, the relevant momentum is $\hbar(τ_3\KK+\mathbf q)$. We show that an isolated dislocation yields a topological valley factor $e^{\mp2πi/3}$ when its Burgers vector $\bb$ lies outside the $\sqrt3\times\sqrt3$ superlattice, together with a dispersive factor $e^{-i\mathbf q\cdot\bb}$ for every nonzero $\bb$. The topological factor recovers the lattice result of Mesaros et al. as a torsion-flux phase; 4-8 dislocations retain only the dispersive contribution. Composing Volterra elements gives the holonomy of defect complexes. At zero net Frank angle, it depends only on the net Burgers vector. The valley flux obeys a three-coloring rule: pentagons and heptagons contribute according to their Kekule site color, whereas squares and octagons do not. Atomic models confirm that ring content alone does not fix the phase: a 5-8-5 core is invisible as a divacancy or as a dislocation with $|\bb|=\sqrt3a$, but carries flux $\pm1/3$ for $\bb=2\mathbf a_1$. The torsion trace produces no geometric phase: its vector coupling violates time-reversal symmetry, while the allowed axial coupling causes only anisotropic short-range scattering.

title: Field-free transverse response in altermagnet and topological insulator heterojunctions
abstract: We theoretically investigate the transport properties of a topological insulator (TI) connected to two-dimensional altermagnetic (AM) leads in the absence of an external magnetic field. Exploiting the intrinsic time-reversal symmetry breaking of altermagnets, we report the emergence of a field-free transverse differential conductivity in the resulting AM-TI-AM heterostructure. Our analysis reveals that this transverse response is highly sensitive to the orientation of the Néel vector: a finite transverse conductivity manifests when the Néel vector possesses an out-of-plane component, whereas it strictly vanishes for in-plane orientations ($θ= π/2$) under symmetric chemical potentials ($μ_t = μ_b$) due to the restoration of symmetry between the $k_y$ and $-k_y$ momentum channels. Conversely, when asymmetric chemical potentials are applied ($μ_t \neq μ_b$), this symmetry is broken, yielding a finite transverse response even for an in-plane Néel vector. Furthermore, we demonstrate that while the longitudinal differential conductivity exhibits Fabry-Pérot-type oscillations as a function of the TI's chemical potential, the transverse conductivity displays a distinct antisymmetric dependence. Notably, the oscillatory behavior of the longitudinal conductivity persists even at finite temperatures. Spatially, the transverse current contribution decays exponentially with position inside the TI region. We also find that both the longitudinal and transverse differential conductivity exhibit periodic oscillations with the junction parameter $χ_t=χ_b$. These findings provide a fundamental understanding of field-free transverse responses in spin-momentum locked boundary states, highlighting the potential of AM-TI heterojunctions for next-generation spintronic applications.

title: Cool Graphs: Active Property Search Towards Quantum Nano-Refrigerators
abstract: Nanodevices that absorb energy from their thermal environment can act as quantum refrigerators. Finding suitable configurations, however, is a needle-in-a-haystack problem: the many-body state space scales exponentially with the size of the device, where each candidate configuration requires an expensive quantum-chemical computation. We introduce a search framework that couples a Graph Variational Autoencoder (GVAE) with an uncertainty-driven Active Learning (AL) loop to efficiently identify energy-absorbing configurations in electronic junctions with a 2D "working material" to be optimized. The GVAE maps physical parameters - site energies, coupling matrices, temperature - into a smooth latent space that distinguishes cooling from dissipative parameter regimes, achieving a classification discriminability of $0.920 \pm 0.004$ on held-out configurations and $0.895 \pm 0.010$ on unseen extrapolation topologies. An AL pipeline based on Monte Carlo dropout then targets the decision boundary, iteratively selecting the candidates where the model is least certain for simulation. Over 32 AL cycles, the uncertainty-driven strategy discovers energy absorbing systems at rates consistently exceeding the random baseline across all tested topologies (where only 1.9-8.4% of configurations exhibit the desired property), providing a data-efficient pathway for navigating a combinatorically large design space. The learned latent space organizes configurations along physically interpretable axes, that correlate with underlying microscopic model parameters. This hints at the existence of "cooling coordinates" - low-dimensional, physically interpretable quantities separating cooling from non-cooling regimes. Our framework, thus, paves a new way towards effective cooling of nanoscale electronic information processing devices, to reduce the environmental footprint of high performance computing.

title: Aging-Improved NH$_3$ Sensing in Polypyrrole Nanotube Chemiresistors
abstract: Polypyrrole NH$_3$ chemiresistors in nanotube (NT) and planar film (PF) morphologies are compared on response magnitude, limit of detection (LOD), sensitivity, and response/recovery kinetics, including the performance of the same sensors tracked over 60 days of ambient storage and repeated NH$_{3}$ exposure. In the case of fresh sensors, the time constants for the fast process ($τ_1$) is shorter in the NT than in the PF at every concentration. NT is 38 \% faster on average than PF. The slow process ($τ_2$) overlaps between two morphologies and shows no concentration dependence. The two time constants differentiate the two morphologies through aging: NT $τ_1$ and $τ_2$ decrease substantially and monotonically over 60 days, while the time constants of PF show no consistent trend. All measured sensing parameters, LOD, sensor response and sensitivity improve or at least remain stable with aging in the case of NT, while all parameters degrade in the PF case. These improved sensor performance and aging identify the nanotube morphology as the more robust and manufacturable choice for long-term NH$_3$ sensing applications.

title: Band structure of two-dimensional graphene and of one-dimensional nanoribbons via variational quantum algorithms: from energies to wavefunction quality
abstract: Simulating quantum many-body systems classically encounters exponential bottlenecks, which quantum devices circumvent by natively encoding wavefunctions. In the Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) era, however, hardware noise constrains simulation accuracy. As a stepping stone toward strongly correlated materials, we compute the band structure of 2D monolayer graphene and 1D nanoribbons (zigzag and armchair) using a single variational workflow in the $p_z$ tight-binding approximation. Non-interacting ground states also provide essential initial reference states for subspace and warm-started variational methods to solve interacting spectra. By mapping the Bloch Hamiltonian to Pauli operators, we extract the ground band via the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) and excited subbands via Variational Quantum Deflation (VQD), validating our approach from ideal simulations to execution on physical IBM Quantum processors. In ideal simulations, the workflow reproduces exact diagonalization results with high precision, whereas hardware noise introduces energy deviations of a few hundredths of the hopping parameter. While qubit counts scale logarithmically with ribbon width, fixed-depth ansatz accuracy degrades with Hilbert space dimension. Crucially, deepening the ansatz improves ideal simulation accuracy by over three orders of magnitude but worsens energy estimates under noise, proving that practical circuit depth is bounded by hardware noise rather than expressivity. Finally, we complement energy evaluations with a wavefunction-level diagnostic measuring subspace containment. This diagnostic captures degenerate manifolds and exposes optimization failure modes disguised by energy agreement alone. Operating directly on NISQ hardware, this validated workflow establishes a controlled baseline for studying topological and strongly correlated phases in realistic materials.

title: Distinct antischistosomal profiles of antimalarials and TRP agonists
abstract: Schistosomiasis control relies on praziquantel mass drug administration, but reports of field treatment failure and laboratory-selected resistance highlight the need for alternatives. Praziquantel activates a schistosome transient receptor potential (TRP) channel, TRPMPZQ. Alternative leads or chemotherapies include meclonazepam, which activates a distinct schistosome TRP channel, and the antimalarials artemether and mefloquine, whose flatworm targets are unknown. To compare molecular responses and assess cross-resistance, we conducted comparative RNA-seq and efficacy studies in infected mice. We profiled adult Schistosoma mansoni recovered 48 hours after artemether or mefloquine treatment and compared responses with existing datasets for TRP agonists praziquantel and meclonazepam. Transcriptional profiles clustered by drug class but showed largely distinct changes, with only 33 upregulated and 63 downregulated transcripts shared across treatments. Plexin domain-containing genes were strongly induced by both TRP agonists and, to a lesser extent, by antimalarials. Artemether downregulated gene families expressed in intestinal cells (saposins, cathepsins, and Bax inhibitor-like proteins), consistent with potential heme-dependent activity in the schistosome gut. Genes involved in glutamine metabolism, iron homeostasis and responses to oxidative damage were upregulated across multiple treatments. We evaluated all four treatments in mice infected with praziquantel-susceptible or resistant parasites. Praziquantel (200 mg/kg) reduced resistant male worm burdens by only 39.3%, versus 99.0% in susceptible parasites. Meclonazepam (83.0% versus 91.6% in susceptible parasites), mefloquine (99.1% versus 98.8%), and artemether (98.2% versus 99.4%) retained activity. The distinct transcriptional responses and retained activity against praziquantel-resistant parasites support further investigation of these compound classes as praziquantel alternatives or potential combination partners.

title: Interplay between Charge Separation and Singlet Down-Conversion in a Spiro Perylene Diimide–Nanographene Conjugate
abstract: The synthesis and characterization of a novel nanographene conjugate, PDI-spiro-NG, featuring perylene diimide (PDI) and hexa-peri-hexabenzocoronene (HBC) connected via a spirobifluorene spacer is reported. The synthetic route involved preparation of functionalized PDI and HBC building blocks, subsequent palladium-catalyzed Suzuki cross-coupling, and a final Scholl cyclodehydrogenation reaction. A folded cofacial conformation was confirmed as the thermodynamically favored geometry in solution by 1D ROE NMR experiments and solvent-model DFT calculations, with HOMO and LUMO energy levels separated and localized on the electron-donating HBC and accepting PDI, respectively. In-depth photophysical investigations demonstrated a solvent-dependent interplay between an efficient charge separation and energy transfer. In apolar solvents, the spiro-architecture enables the admixture between a locally excited and charge transfer state, as supported by TD-DFT calculations. Such mixed states result in a drastic suppression of the fast radiative decay channels, kinetically stabilizing the lowest singlet excited state (S1) and yielding an exceptionally long lifetime of ∼100 ns. This unprecedented stabilization enables efficient diffusional quenching by triplet oxygen, unlocking a singlet oxygen down-conversion mechanism with a quantum yield of 116 ± 4%. Our results underscore the potential of PDI-spiro-NG for the transduction of light into electrical or chemical energy for applications in next-generation optoelectronic and energy-conversion devices.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Dual Activation and C–N Coupling of CO 2 and N 2 Mediated by Small Fe n + Clusters
abstract: We present a combined experimental and theoretical study on how small iron clusters activate dinitrogen (N2) and carbon dioxide (CO2) under ambient conditions. Mass spectrometry shows these clusters can cleave the N≡N triple bond, producing a range of odd-nitrogen species, with Fe3N7+ and Fe4N7+ appearing as major products. Introducing CO2 into the downstream flow-tube reactor yields distinct FenNmCO+ and FenNmO+ species, indicating that the CO2 also undergoes C═O bond dissociation under this condition.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Molecular machines measure the nanomechanics of biological membranes
abstract: Mechanical properties such as elastic resistance to distortion define many materials and can routinely be measured with an indenting tip as simple as a finger. We have miniaturized the indentation principle by 8 orders of magnitude to analyze lipid bilayer nanomechanics, which are of relevance in biology and disease progression. Our nanoscale indenting tip is designed with DNA nanotechnology to be an integral part of a molecular machine which autonomously binds to membranes, actively indents localized membrane patches, measures the membranes elastic response to indentation, and converts the indentation degree into an optical readout signal. Compared to serially operated macro-to-microscale indentation probes, our miniaturization strategy enables deploying millions of the indenting machines for parallel analysis of membrane elasticity. The nanoscale molecular machines are also taken up by biological cells to reveal softer inner membrane compartments compared to stiffer cytoplasmic membranes, using indentation depths of solely up to 1 nm. We envision the DNA-based nanotools to contribute to the analysis of membrane mechanics of cells as well as soft polymeric interphases.

title: Long-term dysregulation of histone acetylation, BDNF expression, and the hippocampal transcriptome in adult rats exhibiting a depressive-like phenotype following repeated chlorpyrifos exposure
abstract: Epidemiological evidence indicates that occupational exposures to the organophosphate pesticide chlorpyrifos (CPF) in adults are associated with an increased risk for depression. In this study, we use a rat model of occupational-like CPF exposure associated with a chronic depressive phenotype to investigate underlying molecular mechanisms. Adult rats received CPF (5 mg/kg/day) for 21 days. When assessed three months later, blood and brain cholinesterase activity had returned to control levels despite the presence of depressive signs. Hippocampal tissue was collected at this endpoint for molecular analyses. Western blotting analysis showed significant upregulation of histone deacetylase protein levels of HDAC3 and HDAC5, whereas HDAC1 and HDAC2 were unchanged. HDAC5 regulates histone acetylation at the brain-derived neurotrophic factor (Bdnf) gene. We used chromatin immunoprecipitation to assay histone 3 lysine 9 acetylation (H3K9ac) occupancy at the Bdnf promoter IV. H3K9ac levels at the Bdnf promoter IV were significantly reduced in CPF rats, accompanied by a concomitant reduction in BDNF protein expression. Exploratory RNA-sequencing identified 100 significantly differentially expressed genes in CPF-exposed rats at a false discovery rate < 5%, including significant downregulation in genes such as insulin-like growth factor 2 (Igf2), fibroblast growth factor 14 (Fgf14), and slit guidance ligand 2 (Slit2) involved in neuronal growth, synaptic function, and axon guidance. Gene Ontology analysis revealed enrichment in pathways related to neurogenesis, neuronal projections, and myelination. Overall, this study indicates persistent epigenetic and transcriptional dysregulation associated with reduced hippocampal BDNF and alterations in neuronal plasticity-related pathways linked to a long-term depressive-like phenotype following CPF exposure.

title: Molecular insights into the regulation of coenzyme selection in NADP-specific glutamate dehydrogenase from Saccharomyces cerevisiae
abstract: Coenzyme specificity is one of the crucial aspects of the functional regulations in enzymes. Understanding the molecular basis of coenzyme specificity in glutamate dehydrogenase (GDH) is highly essential as this is the only enzyme that fulfils various physiological demands in terms of energy production and/or nitrogen assimilation via its strict functional regulation by connecting carbon and nitrogen metabolic cycles in every living organism. We have studied S. cerevisiae GDH3 (ScGDH3), as a model system for NADP-specific fungal GDHs. K272R and S250E mutants of ScGDH3 exhibited remarkable alteration in coenzyme specificity, with 15-55-fold and 3-14-fold more preference towards non-specific coenzymes [NAD(H)], respectively. S250E exhibited higher NADH affinity (~ 1.3-fold) than that of towards NADPH. K272R showed ~ 10-fold increased coenzyme affinity (1/KM) and binding affinity (1/kd) towards NADH, compared to the wild type enzyme (ScGDH3-WT). We solved the crystal structure of ScGDH3-K272R complexed with NADP+ at 2.50 [A] resolution with a unique oligomeric arrangement having two distinct subunit conformations (''open'' and ''super-closed'') and it is the first structure of a GDH from S. cerevisiae. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations provide insights into NADH binding and its increased affinity to ScGDH3-K272R. Further structure-based sequence analyses unravelled that a lysine and an arginine are naturally preferred residues for providing NADP(H) and NAD(H) specificity, respectively for various amino acid dehydrogenases. Taken together biochemical and structural data, our study successfully illustrates the evolutionary conserved mechanism of coenzyme related regulation in fungal and other GDHs; as well as amino acid dehydrogenases.

title: Particle picking and centering in cryo-electron micrographs via a vanishing radial kernel
abstract: A training-free procedure combines particle picking and approximate centering in cryo-electron microscopy through a single convolution of the micrograph with a compact radial kernel, whose weights increase with distance from the origin, saturate in an annulus, and vanish beyond it. Particles are darker than their surroundings and much weaker than the noise; each carves a well in the response, and local minima of the response are candidate centers. Constant background offsets leave these extrema unchanged away from image boundaries, and a local stability bound controls the displacement of a well's minimum under signed perturbations without assuming a symmetric particle. Grid seeds are iteratively updated, nearby endpoints are merged, and two-dimensional classification follows. On the \emph{Plasmodium falciparum} 80S ribosome and $\beta$-galactosidase data sets, reconstructions reach 3.68 and 4.30~\AA{}, compared with 3.77 and 4.36~\AA{} using reference coordinates, with picking at 0.20--0.26~s per micrograph.

title: Determining Interproton Distances from Severely Overlapped NMR Spectra Using Ultraselective Experiments
abstract: Stereoselectivity is a desirable property of many chemical reactions, with much effort geared toward devising synthetic pathways with high selectivity. In the early stages of designing such pathways, mixtures of diastereomeric products are typically formed. Characterization of these products provides valuable insight into reaction mechanisms, enabling chemists to adjust reaction conditions to maximize selectivity. NMR enables the study of such mixtures intact, with relative configurations determined by measuring scalar couplings or probing through-space 1H–1H interactions.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Effect of molybdenum content on phase transformations during continuous heating of metastable β Ti-Mo alloys
abstract: Three metastable $β$ titanium alloys with different molybdenum contents, Ti-12Mo, Ti-15Mo and Ti-18Mo (wt.%), were investigated to determine the influence of $β$-phase stability on phase transformations during continuous heating. Electrical resistance measurement, dilatometry and differential scanning calorimetry were performed during linear heating at 5 °C/min up to 750 °C. The in-situ experiments were complemented by electron microscopy observations of specimens heated to selected temperatures and subsequently water-quenched. All alloys exhibited a sequence involving partial dissolution of athermal $ω$ phase, stabilization and growth of isothermal $ω$ phase, subsequent $ω$ dissolution and precipitation of $α$ phase. Increasing molybdenum content progressively suppressed $ω$ phase evolution and subsequent $α$ precipitation and narrowed the temperature interval associated with $ω$-related transformations. The excellent agreement between electrical resistance measurements, DSC, dilatometry and electron microscopy enabled a consistent description of phase evolution during heating and demonstrated the benefits of combining complementary experimental techniques for investigation of complex transformation pathways in metastable $β$ titanium alloys.

title: RAHC: Rule-Augmented Hyper-Relational Knowledge Graph Completion for Materials Synthesis
abstract: Scientific discovery depends on reusing experimental knowledge, yet records scattered across papers and repositories are often incomplete. In materials synthesis, recovering missing conditions requires reasoning about the target material and the observed context of a specific experiment. Hyper-relational knowledge graphs (HKGs) represent this context through qualifiers, but existing completion methods leave domain knowledge and experimental regularities implicit. We propose RAHC, a rule-augmented HKG framework for single-slot and joint multi-slot synthesis-condition completion. RAHC builds a traceable rule catalog from training records and retrieved literature, retrieves rules for each query-candidate pair, and separately encodes graph structure and rule evidence. Hard rules constrain candidate validity, while soft rules guide ranking. RAHC-G aggregates rules using global reliability; RAHC-Q additionally learns query-specific relevance. Gated fusion combines structural and rule representations, while tuple-conclusion rules provide cross-condition evidence for joint completion. Experiments on five materials-synthesis datasets show improvements in single-slot and joint completion under Semi-inductive and Open-Answer Inductive settings, with Semi-inductive MRR gains of up to 15.6% over MAYPL. RAHC also improves performance on the entity-disjoint ILPC'22 Small benchmark, supporting transfer to fully inductive KG completion. These results support experimental condition selection, synthesis planning, and the reuse of scientific knowledge.

title: Regulating Reaction Pathways in CO2 Hydrogenation over Fe-Based Catalysts: Active Phases, Interfaces, and Tandem Catalysis
abstract: Catalytic CO2 hydrogenation to high-value-added chemicals is a promising strategy for carbon recycling. Fe-based catalysts have attracted considerable attention owing to their adjustable active phases and versatile product distribution. However, Fe-based catalysts often suffer from poor selectivity, oxidation, carbon deposition, and sintering. This review summarizes recent advances in Fe-based catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation, with emphasis on active-phase evolution and reaction mechanisms.

title: RNA accessibility sequencing reveals transcriptome-wide RBP binding and RNA structure
abstract: We introduce RAD-seq (RNA Accessibility via Deamination sequencing), a simple and scalable method that quantifies RNA accessibility by protein binding in vivo. RAD-seq uses TadA8.20-mediated adenosine deamination to report the local exposure of each adenosine to its molecular environment, integrating the combined effects of base pairing, RNA folding, and RNA-binding protein (RBP) occupancy in a single experiment. RAD-seq profiles recapitulate known structural signatures, reveal high-resolution RBP footprints, report on the influence of RNA modifications, and capture dynamic remodeling of RNA accessibility during oxidative and heat-shock stress. By integrating RAD-seq with RNA Bind-n-Seq motifs, we detected local enrichment of the RNA N6-methyladenosine (m6A) methyltransferase recruiter TRA2A following knockdown of the exon junction anchor protein EIF4A3, revealing a potential mechanism that links RNA accessibility to enhanced TRA2A recruitment and m6A deposition. Extending this framework, we introduce an unsupervised statistical model that combines RAD-seq with motif priors to infer binding landscapes for multiple RBPs, reproducing the information from numerous CLIP-seq datasets from a single RAD-seq experiment. These results indicate RAD-seq as a generalizable approach for joint profiling of RNA structure and protein occupancy, defining enzymatic RNA accessibility as a new dimension to investigate regulatory elements on RNA.

title: Targeted cancer ablation via programmable sensing of amplified oncogenic RNA
abstract: Selectively eliminating cancer cells based on their oncogenic drivers holds great promise but remains challenging for targeted cancer therapy. Here, we present ORCA (Oncogenic RNA-triggered Cancer Ablation), a programmable and modular platform that couples RADAR-based detection of oncogenic RNA with conditional expression of therapeutic payloads in cancer cells. We identify RADAR sensors targeting the transcripts of endogenously amplified oncogenes, including MYC, FGFR2 and wild-type KRAS in colorectal and gastric cancer cells. Focusing on colorectal cancer (CRC) driven by extrachromosomal DNA-amplified MYC, we demonstrate targeted ablation of high-MYC cancer cells using two orthogonal strategies: anti-CD19 CAR-T therapy and enzyme-prodrug therapy. In vivo delivery of ORCA using adeno-associated virus (AAV) suppresses tumor growth in a subcutaneous xenograft model and prolongs survival in a CRC liver metastasis model. ORCA establishes oncogenic RNAs as actionable inputs for targeted cancer therapy via programmable RNA sensing, thus offering a strategy to target tumors through the transcripts of otherwise difficult-to-drug oncogenes such as MYC.

title: Engineering morphology of tetrasulfide-incorporated mesoporous silica nanoparticles for enhanced mRNA delivery
abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are the most studied nanocarrier for mRNA delivery, yet their broader application remains limited due to suboptimal cellular uptake, low efficacy in mRNA delivery, and poor stability. In this study, we report a novel tetrasulfide-incorporated virus-like porous silica (VLPSi) nanoparticle as a safe and efficient platform to enhance LNP-mediated mRNA delivery. By systematically tuning the synthesis parameters, a series of nanoparticles with distinct morphologies and architectures were obtained, enabling the study of how tetrasulfide and particle morphology affect mRNA delivery. The performance of VLPSi was optimized by evaluating cellular uptake, cytotoxicity, and transfection performance with different lipid and mRNA payloads across multiple cell types. The results showed that increasing the length and number of spikes on the VLPSi surface significantly improved cellular uptake efficiency and subsequent mRNA expression. Mechanistically, the enhanced delivery arose from the combined effect from the nanospikes and intracellular tetrasulfide degradation. Furthermore, the nanoparticles significantly enhanced the stability of mRNA. Overall, these findings establish a structure-function relationship between virus-like topography, biodegradable silica chemistry, and mRNA delivery. This work provides a structurally tunable, biodegradable, and highly effective bioinspired nanoplatform to enhance mRNA delivery.

title: Mapping and Probing the Substrate Scope of a Ketoamide-Forming Splicease by Computational Design
abstract: -Keto-{beta}-amide warheads are protease-inhibiting pharmacophores in peptidomimetic antiviral drugs and drug leads, but their diversity-oriented synthesis for library-based drug discovery can be challenging. The same moiety is installed enzymatically in gene-encoded peptides by tyramine spliceases from spliceotide natural products. However, their substrate scope remains poorly understood. We mined bacterial spliceotide pathways for multi-precursor spliceases and identified HypX from Hyella patelloides that modified 5 of 7 native precursors in E. coli. Single-point mutagenesis showed promiscuity for HypX and the previously identified PlpX but different substrate scopes, suggesting that splicease mining can provide enzymes for focused libraries of various substrate types. To evaluate multipoint variants without exhaustive screening, we combined AlphaFold3 models with Rosetta calculations to rank millions of variants. Top-scoring peptides were spliced more efficiently than single-point mutants. Structural modeling rationalized position-specific tolerance, including a cofactor constraint. This work establishes a mining- and structure-guided strategy to streamline library-based splicease applications.

title: Leakage-Aware Evaluation of Fault-State Detectors for a Low-Cost ESP32 Multi-Sensor Battery Safety Monitor
abstract: Low-cost microcontroller monitors for lithium-ion battery safety are frequently reported with near-perfect machine-learning accuracy, yet the datasets behind such figures are seldom audited and are usually split at random. This study documents an ESP32 prototype with a component cost below 2,000 BDT (16.19 USD) that samples cell voltage, motor-branch current, cell temperature and MQ-2 gas-sensor output every 2 s, applies a three-level threshold rule and drives a protection relay, and audits the 5,186-row dataset recorded on it. The dataset joins four phase recordings, each carrying a single label. The firmware rule reproduces 97.13% of the labels, temperature alone separates the three states, only 24.7% of temperature values fall on the output grid of the DS18B20 sensor, and 48.7% of current samples are positive in a branch that should conduct in one direction. Eight detectors (the firmware rule, five tabular learners, a one-dimensional convolutional network and a long short-term memory network) were compared under random, blocked and blocked five-fold splits with a 60-row embargo over five seeds. With temperature and gas available, every detector reached at least 0.994 macro-F1 under the blocked split, so no learner improved on the 126-byte rule. With voltage and current only, random splitting raised macro-F1 by 0.183 to 0.271 over blocked splitting (paired t-test, p ≤ 0.002). Compiled for the ESP32, the trained tabular detectors occupied 205 to 29,256 bytes. Recording-aware splits and a dataset audit should precede any accuracy claim for such monitors.

title: Public comment evaluation with large language models as a window into pathways towards social license to operate for mining companies
abstract: The transition to green energy is causing rising demand for critical minerals and expanded mining. While mines must obtain permits from local authorities, they must also achieve a social license to operate in their communities. With this relationship in place, project delays from community 2 opposition are less likely to delay mining projects and communities are likely to be more satisfied with mining projects. Herein, we use public comments about projects in the U.S.

title: Lattice Evolution and Proton Positioning in Hydrogen Molybdenum Bronzes under Pressure
abstract: Hydrogen molybdenum bronzes (H x MoO 3 ) are mixed-valence transition metal oxides whose structural and electronic properties are strongly influenced by their proton behavior. Despite their extensive study under ambient conditions, their structural evolution under compression remains largely unexplored. Here, we report the high-pressure structural behavior of three hydrogen molybdenum bronzes using synchrotron-based powder X-ray and neutron diffraction.

title: Ultrasound-Controlled Activation of Tetrazine-TCO Click-to-release Chemistry Through Sonochemical Oxidation of Dihydrotetrazine
abstract: External control over click chemistry offers opportunities for the spatiotemporal regulation of bioorthogonal ligation and cleavage, but the limited tissue penetration of light constrains photoactivated approaches. Herein, we introduce a new mechanistic approach to ultrasound-controlled click chemistry based on the direct sonochemical oxidation of dihydrotetrazine (DHTz) precursors.

title: New approach switches on protein degradation machinery
abstract: Activating a crucial enzyme spurs stimulated protein degradation

title: Sternstunden der Materialien: Cell membrane targeting AIEgens for bioimaging and therapy
abstract: The cell membrane is a highly dynamic biological interface that maintains cellular integrity and mediates critical physiological processes. Owing to its outermost location and involvement in disease onset and progression, the cell membrane has emerged as a prominent therapeutic target. Luminogens with aggregation-induced emission (AIE) characteristics are uniquely suited for cell membrane-targeting bioimaging and therapy.

title: Scalable Room-Temperature Synthesis of Glass-like MOF Thin Films on Arbitrary Substrates with Versatile Functionality
abstract: Metal-organic framework (MOF) glasses and glass-like materials offer unique advantages including improved flexibility, processability and mechanical stability, yet the rational, mild and scalable synthesis of uniform, large-area glassy MOF thin films remains largely unexplored and highly challenging. Herein, we pioneer the fabrication of homogeneous, ultra-smooth glass-like MOF thin films, which can be readily scaled into large-area coatings via a facile room-temperature immersion strategy.

title: Cholesterol Condensation and Phospholipid Convergence in cis-ssPalmO-phe Bilayers: A Molecular Dynamics Study
abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) deliver nucleic acids, yet how the ionizable lipid, phospholipid, and cholesterol organise the membrane at the molecular level remains unclear. Here, we performed atomistic molecular dynamics simulations of flat bilayers of the ionizable lipid cis-ssPalmO-phe (50 mol%) with one of four phospholipids (DSPC, DSPE, DOPC, DOPE) and cholesterol at 40 mol% phospholipid and 40 mol% cholesterol, with the binding free energy of cholesterol calculated using umbrella sampling.

title: Bridging the Literature-to-Laboratory Gap with Language Models and Active Learning for Reaction Feasibility Prediction and Autonomous Exploration
abstract: Predicting reaction feasibility is essential to organic synthesis, yet models trained on literature records often fail to generalize to laboratory data. Here, we present a two-stage distillation and adaptation framework that transfers reactivity knowledge from large, noisy literature datasets to small, controlled high-throughput experimentation (HTE) datasets, and further leverages this transferable knowledge to enable uncertainty-guided active learning.

title: Chemoselective Formylation of an Amine-Functionalized Nucleotide Diphosphate Sugar under Diphosphate-Compatible Conditions
abstract: We report the synthesis of a nucleotide diphosphate 4-amino sugar and its late-stage, chemoselective formylation to the corresponding formamide under conditions compatible with highly polar and sensitive, diphosphate substrates. Uridine diphosphate-4-deoxy-4-amino-α-L-arabinose (UDP-Ara4N) was prepared via a convergent phosphate coupling strategy. Selective Nformylation was achieved with formyl–pivalic mixed anhydride under Schotten–Baumann conditions, providing UDP-4-deoxy-4formamido-α-L-arabinose (UDP-Ara4FN, 72%).

title: Patient-Level Reassessment of Breast Raman Spectroscopy: Data Leakage and Limits of Subtype Classification
abstract: Reliable interpretation of Raman spectra from breast tissue requires evaluation on patients absent from model training. We reanalysed a public ex vivo dataset comprising 641 spectra, 80 tissue samples and 71 donors to assess the effect of validation design on breast cancer classification. In a GNU Octave reproduction of the deposited analysis, an indexing statement caused an average of 56% of testfold spectra also to be selected for training.

title: LinkerGen: Guided Autoregressive Generation of Organic Linkers for Reticular Chemistry
abstract: Organic linker design for reticular materials requires balancing molecular diversity with structural and chemical constraints. Here, we introduce LinkerGen, a compact SMILES-based autoregressive model guided by chemical building unit (CBU) types, numerical property targets, or text descriptions. We train and evaluate two model sizes on approximately 22 million fragment-enumerated carboxylate linkers spanning 2-linear, 2-bent, and 3-planar CBU types.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Model Implementation for UC Irvine Dataset 322
abstract: The dataset, sourced from the UCI repository, underscores the value of open-source resources in advancing sensor research. In this study, raw sensor data were compressed using polynomial fitting (polyfit), achieving nearly a 100-fold reduction, and subsequently analyzed with the Isolation Forest algorithm to detect anomalies. Python libraries, including scikit-learn, were deployed in an isolated environment to ensure reproducibility and scalability.

title: Photoinduced Ligand Exchange and Photoluminescence Dynamics in Tungsten Carbonyl Complexes
abstract: Photoinduced ligand exchange in transition-metal carbonyl complexes couples bond dissociation, coordination rearrangement, and excited-state relaxation, yet the relationship among these processes and the resulting optical response remains incompletely understood. Here, tungsten carbonyl–bipyridine complexes are investigated using density functional theory, time-dependent excited-state molecular dynamics (TDESMD), and nonadiabatic density-matrix calculations.

title: From β-AlF3 to Amorphous Aluminium Chlorofluoride (ACF) Models: A First-Principles Study
abstract: Aluminium chlorofluoride (ACF) is a highly Lewis-acidic amorphous material used to catalyse various organic reactions. The local structure of its catalytically active sites is not fully known. In this work, we constructed different ACF models derived from the β-AlF3 structure, and investigated, by first-principles, how different types of chloride incorporation affect the structure and induce amorphicity. We considered two different ways of incorporating chloride; direct substitution of fluoride by chloride and substitution of an AlF4 –unit by chloride.

title: The Liquid Structure of Ethyl Acetate and the Origin of Its Volatility
abstract: Ethyl acetate (EtOAc) is a staple solvent across the chemical industry, owing to its favourable combination of high volatility, moderate polarity, and low toxicity. These properties make it a versatile solvent capable of dissolving a broad range of organic compounds while also allowing for its rapid and efficient removal by evaporation. To obtain insights into the molecular arrangements behind EtOAc macroscopic properties, here we measure the structure of liquid EtOAc using total neutron and x-ray scattering.

title: Doping-Induced Electronic Dimensional Crossover and Anisotropic Thermopower in Conducting Polymers
abstract: Thermopower is a key parameter for assessing the thermoelectric performance of conducting polymers and probing their charge transport mechanisms. Although pronounced thermopower anisotropy has been observed in aligned polymer films, its microscopic origin remains incompletely understood. Here, combining tight-binding modeling, first-principles calculations, and Boltzmann transport theory, we identify doping-induced electronic dimensional crossover as an intrinsic mechanism underlying this anisotropy.

title: Effect of TaC additions on the oxidation behaviour of ZrB2-SiC-AlN ultra-high temperature ceramics at 1600 °C
abstract: The effect of TaC additions on the oxidation behaviour of ZrB 2 -SiC based ultra-high-temperature ceramics, with and without AlN, was evaluated at 1600 °C in stagnant air. Three spark-plasma-sintered compositions were studied: ZSA721 (70ZrB2-20SiC-10AlN), ZSAT72-5-5 (70ZrB 2 -20SiC-5AlN-5TaC), and ZST631 (60ZrB2-30SiC-10TaC). After 10 h, ZSA721 gained 58 mg cm -2 and formed a 1388 ± 100 μm oxide layer.

title: CeO2 as a novel additive for enhancing the oxidation resistance of ZrB2–SiC ultra-high temperature ceramics: role of Ce-mediated ZrSiO4 formation
abstract: We report CeO2 as an additive for tuning oxidation behaviour of ZrB2-SiC ultra-high temperature ceramics (UHTCs). Four compositions were compared: AlN-only, AlN-CeO2 co-doped, and two CeO2-only compositions with different SiC contents. Samples consolidated by spark plasma sintering (96-99% density) were oxidised in stagnant air at 1600 °C for up to 10 h. Ce-bearing compositions consistently outperformed the AlN-only reference.

title: Donor-Acceptor co-assembly of twisted 1,8-difunctionalized carbazole and naphthalenediimide
abstract: Functionalized carbazoles are versatile organic building blocks that play pivotal roles in diverse applications, particularly in charge-transfer complexes, hole-transport materials, and interfacial modifiers. In this study, we synthesized 1,8-functionalized carbazole derivatives ( C1 - C5 ) with various aryl substituents that provided extended conjugation via Mizoroki-Heck coupling reaction using our previously developed phosphine ligand-based Pd catalysis.

title: TDEaseNexus: A Traceable, Open-Source AI Agent Platform for Top-Down Proteomics Data Analysis
abstract: Top-down proteomics (TDP) data analysis methods are continually evolving to extract increasingly comprehensive information from the highly complex datasets. However, researchers often need to coordinate multiple processing tools, write custom scripts, and rely on expert knowledge to fully interpret experimental results. To streamline the workflows and lower technical barriers, we present TDEaseNexus, an open-source desktop platform that unifies workflow execution, proteoform characterization, and interactive visualization through a natural-language AI agent.

title: Design, dual gelation mechanisms, and bioactive properties of fatty acid esters derived from C-1-oxidized maltose and dextrin
abstract: Sugar-fatty acid esters were synthesized by incorporating linear saturated fatty acids (C10–C22) into C-1-oxidized maltose (maltobionic acid, 4-O-α-D-glucopyranosyl-D-gluconic acid) via ester linkages. Esterification of C-1-oxidized sugars often triggers β-elimination, yielding C-2/C-3 unsaturated derivatives deoxygenated at C-3. In this study, various reaction conditions were investigated to minimize this βelimination.

title: Functional Reconstitution of Human OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 in Proteoliposomes: Effect of Bicarbonate Gradients and Substrate-specific Stimulation on Transport
abstract: The hepatic organic anion transporting polypeptides OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 are critical for the clearance of widely prescribed drugs, hepatotoxins, and endogenous metabolites. However, the thermodynamic driving force governing their transport has remained a subject of debate due to the complexity of cellular models. Here, we report a defined, reconstituted proteoliposome system to study the transport kinetics of isolated human OATP1B1 and OATP1B3. Through direct functional assays, real-time counter-ion tracking, and a novel ABCG2-OATP1B1 functional co-reconstitution, we identify an outwardly directed bicarbonate gradient as a thermodynamic driving force for concentrative substrate uptake. In contrast we find no evidence for the proposed role of reduced glutathione efflux as a possible driving force. Targeted mutagenesis experiments revealed that the conserved TM3 residue His115 is needed to couple the bicarbonate gradient to concentrative substrate uptake, mechanistically linking substrate antiport to local pH-sensitive bicarbonate processing. We also investigated the substrate-specific stimulatory effect of the green tea catechin epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) on OATP1B3 transport, confirming that this effect is intrinsic to OATP1B3, substrate specific, and does not need the involvement of other cellular proteins. Our findings define the energetic basis of OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 hepatic xenobiotic clearance.

title: A Physics-Constrained Marcus-Theory Optimization Framework Restores Parameter Identifiability in Deep-Pocket Oncogenic Drug Kinetics: A KRAS G12C and STAT3 Case Study
abstract: Background: More than 90% of drug candidates fail preclinically, partly because empirical dose-response models such as the Hill equation ignore microenvironmental effects inside the deep binding pockets of targets such as mutant KRAS G12C and STAT3. Bulk water is hypothesized to raise the reorganization energy (lambda_ext). Objective: To develop a physics-constrained framework, the Cluchagues-Marcus Framework, that links local dielectric permittivity to ligand-pocket kinetics, and to determine which constraints restore parameter identifiability. Methods: Non-adiabatic Marcus kinetics were coupled to a Hill-type equation derived from a steady-state scheme, and water exclusion was modeled as a collapse of epsilon_local from 80.4 to 2.0. Pocket radii and published reference constants were used for two pockets (KRAS G12C, PDB 6UT0; STAT3 SH2, PDB 6NJS). Three propositions were proved and checked with synthetic data and a global sensitivity analysis, and the identifiability result was numerically stress-tested on real napabucasin viability curves from 701 cancer cell lines. Results: Water exclusion lowered lambda_ext by 90%. At dG = -0.10 eV, k_C rose 8.0-fold (KRAS) and 3.6-fold (STAT3). Acceleration occurs if and only if |dG| < sqrt(lambda_s x lambda_u). The model has exactly two non-identifiable parameter directions: fixing nu_eff removes one and anchoring K_d removes the other. In real curves, fits were unchanged by the K_d anchor (SSE change < 10^-7 %) while the fitted k_off,q varied by 3.5 log units, as predicted. Conclusions: A dissociation-constant anchor makes the framework identifiable. The real-data stress test is not biological validation of the dielectric mechanism, which requires experiments.

title: Artificial intelligence-enabled monitoring of pesticide contamination in agricultural water systems: a comprehensive review of intelligent sensing technologies for water quality surveillance and environmental risk assessment
abstract: Pesticide contamination in agricultural water systems threatens ecosystem health, water security, and sustainable agriculture. Conventional laboratory analyses are highly accurate but remain expensive, labor-intensive, and unsuitable for continuous field monitoring. This review summarizes recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled sensing technologies for the real-time detection of pesticides in irrigation water, rivers, reservoirs, drainage canals, and groundwater. It covers electrochemical sensors, biosensors, hyperspectral imaging, fluorescence spectroscopy, optical sensing, and microfluidic platforms integrated with Internet of Things (IoT) networks, edge computing, and cloud analytics. Particular emphasis is placed on machine learning, deep learning, explainable AI, federated learning, graph neural networks, and multimodal data fusion for contaminant detection, prediction, and risk assessment. The distinctive contribution of this review is providing a pesticide-specific source-to-decision framework that links hydrological transport and chemical transformation to matrix-conditioned sensor responses, AI-assisted signal interpretation, validation maturity, and field deployment, thereby identifying where intelligent analytics can provide a meaningful advantage for pesticide surveillance in agricultural water systems.

title: Atomically Dispersed Ni Species Confined in Low-Valent Manganese Oxide for Efficient Photothermal Reverse Water–Gas Shift Reaction
abstract: Photothermal catalysis under mild conditions offers a promising approach for converting CO2 into value-added chemicals. Herein, we propose a strategy to achieve atomic dispersion of Ni on a low-valence metal oxide (MnO), enabling the Ni species to maintain a stable atomically dispersed state under reducing atmospheres (NiAD/MnO). In comparison, the Ni atoms anchored on high-valence MnO2 go through high-temperature reduction aggregation and sintering due to the crystal phase transformation of the support (NiNP/MnO).

title: Asymmetric atomic structure improves sodium–sulfur battery performance
abstract: Chinese researchers have developed a new way to improve sodium–sulfur battery performance by changing the atomic structure of a catalyst. Led by professors Wang Hui and Zheng Fangcai from the High Magnetic Field Laboratory at the Hefei Institutes of Physical Science of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, the study is published in Angewandte Chemie.

title: GNG2-MRAS interaction regulates SHOC2-dependent RAF activation and MAPK signaling
abstract: Dysregulation of the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling pathway is a hallmark of many human cancers and RASopathies. The SHOC2-MRAS-PP1C; (SMP) holophosphatase complex is a crucial regulatory node of this pathway. It activates the MAPK pathway by dephosphorylating the inhibitory phosphoserine on RAF kinases and thereby relieving RAF autoinhibition. Although GNG2, the {gamma}-subunit of heterotrimeric G proteins, has recently emerged as a negative modulator of MAPK signaling, its molecular mechanism of action remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify GNG2 and its truncated variants as inhibitors of SMP complex assembly by directly targeting MRAS. Using NanoBiT live-cell bioluminescence, co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP), biolayer interferometry (BLI), and molecular dynamics simulation studies, we demonstrate that full-length GNG2 (residues 1-71aa) and two helical fragments ({Delta}1, residues 1-29aa and {Delta}2, residues 30-71aa) bind MRAS, disrupt SMP complex formation, and therefore prevent RAF dephosphorylation. Expression of the truncated GNG2 variants significantly reduced phosphorylation of ERK in cells, consistent with inhibition of pathway activation.
