Furthermore, a short peptide synthesized from the GNG2 {Delta}2 sequence effectively disrupted SMP complex formation in both purified protein systems and live cells and potently attenuated MAPK signaling. Molecular dynamics simulation studies revealed that GNG2 variants engage with the Switch I/II regions of MRAS, sterically interfering with SHOC2-PP1C association. Together, these findings establish GNG2 as a direct regulator of SMP complex assembly and demonstrate that GNG2-derived peptides represent a promising strategy for disrupting SHOC2-MRAS interactions and suppressing MAPK signaling in RAS/RAF-driven pathologies.

title: Direct Bioconjugations of Diverse Payloads using an Extraordinarily Donor-Promiscuous Flavin Transferase
abstract: Site-specific protein conjugation is a widely used tool in chemical biology research and is the foundation of many biotechnological and biomedical applications. A key enabling technology are repurposed post-translational protein modifying enzymes, where variants with broad donor and acceptor substrate promiscuity were developed into general-purpose bioconjugation platforms. However, direct enzymatic attachment of bulky or structurally diverse payloads is often limited by low reaction efficiencies and difficulties in preparing suitable donors. Consequently, conjugation typically relies on two-step strategies in which an enzyme first installs a bioorthogonal handle on the target protein, followed by chemical attachment of the payload. These enzyme-first, chemistry-second approaches limit chemistry to bioorthogonal reactions that leave a molecular footprint. Here, we introduce direct ADDing, an enzymatic bioconjugation platform based on our discovery of the exceptional donor promiscuity of the flavin transferase ApbE. We show that ApbE accepts a remarkably broad range of donor substrates provided they carry an adenosine diphosphate (ADP) anchor. The prevalence of ADP-containing compounds in nature provides access to diverse building blocks and an extensive biochemical toolbox for donor generation. Exploiting these resources, we demonstrate multiple strategies for preparing compatible donors and achieve direct, site-specific enzymatic conjugation of diverse small molecules, peptides, proteins, and synthetic polymers.

title: Characterizing the Metabolic Fate and Pharmacokinetics of the RyR2 Inhibitor ent-Verticilide
abstract: ent-Verticilide is a synthetic macrocyclic depsipeptide and ryanodine receptor 2 (RyR2) inhibitor with potential therapeutic applications in cardiac arrhythmias. This study characterized its in vitro metabolism and in vivo pharmacokinetics to better understand factors that may influence its disposition. Metabolic stability was evaluated in mouse, rat, dog, and human liver S9 fractions, followed by CYP reaction phenotyping in human liver microsomes and metabolite profiling in human and rat liver S9 fractions. Pharmacokinetics were evaluated in rats following intravenous and oral administration. ent-Verticilide underwent rapid, NADPH-dependent depletion across all species, with in vitro half-lives ranging from 2.1 to 5.3 min. CYP reaction phenotyping indicated that CYP3A was the predominant CYP subfamily involved in its metabolism. Eight putative metabolites were identified in human and rat liver S9, primarily resulting from hydroxylation, oxidation, and desaturation, with generally similar metabolite profiles between species. In rats, ent-verticilide exhibited a systemic clearance of 29.6 mL/min/kg, a steady-state volume of distribution of 4.86 L/kg, and a terminal half-life of 6.85 h following intravenous administration. Absolute oral bioavailability was 10.5%. Overall, these findings show that ent-verticilide undergoes extensive oxidative hepatic metabolism and provide an initial DMPK framework for its continued preclinical development.

title: Sex shapes plasma molecular signatures of dementia risk across APOE ε4 strata
abstract: Sex and APOE ε4 influence dementia risk, but whether its molecular predictors differ across sex and APOE ε4 strata remains unclear. We investigated plasma proteomic and metabolomic signatures predicting future dementia in 43,759 UK Biobank participants across four sex-by-APOE ε4 groups. The association between APOE ε4 carrier status and dementia differed by sex (interaction p = 0.027). Machine-learning models achieved higher discrimination in APOE ε4 carriers (AUC 0.85-0.90) than non-carriers (AUC 0.74-0.76), with the highest performance in female carriers.

title: Gentamicin impairs nephron development in iPSC-derived kidney organoids and disrupts proximal tubular lysosomal function
abstract: Gentamicin is an aminoglycoside antibiotic used to treat Gram-negative bacterial infections. However, its clinical use is limited by nephrotoxicity, affecting approximately 10 - 20% of treated patients. Nevertheless, gentamicin remains widely used due to its high potency, low cost, and low incidence of bacterial resistance and hypersensitivity. Importantly, gentamicin crosses the placental barrier and is administered to neonates, including preterm infants in whom nephrogenesis is still ongoing, raising concerns about its effects on kidney development.

title: Oxidative Nucleophilic Aromatic ipso-Substitution for the Late-Stage Functionalization of Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons with Five-Membered Rings
abstract: Nanographenes and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) are promising materials for advanced organic electronics, but their late-stage functionalization remains challenging. Here, we report an ipso-substitution, in which tert-butyl groups, which are usually installed for solubility reasons, are selectively replaced by mesylates on PAHs and nanographenes bearing five-membered rings. The reaction proceeds via an oxidative nucleophilic aromatic substitution mechanism and can be implemented in oxidative cyclodehydrogenation protocols to produce substituted PAH skeletons in one pot.

title: Fe-Mediated Hydrofluorination of Piperidines: Access towards Fluorinated Iminosugars
abstract: Late-stage hydrofluorination provides access to fluorinated bioactive compounds suitable for 19 F NMR monitoring of biological processes. We report Fe(III)-mediated radical hydrofluorination of highly substituted, chiral N -heterocycles containing piperidine, indolizidine and pyrrolidine scaffolds to the Markovnikov products. This method tolerated steric bulky substrates as well as substituents on nitrogen with different electronic effects. Finally, an Fe(III) catalytic system was compared with Co(II) and Ni(II) catalysts.

title: FROST II: certified Hartree–Fock limits of the closed-shell atoms from neon to xenon
abstract: We extend FROST (Fock radial orbital shooting with Taylor series) from atoms whose occupied orbitals are all s orbitals to closed-shell atoms with p and d shells, and report rigorous upper bounds on the Hartree–Fock (HF) energies of the closed-shell atoms from neon to xenon. Their leading digits are correct to 504 significant figures for neon, 103 for magnesium, 105 for argon and 103–106 for the heavier atoms, against previous records of 30 and 25. Three changes to the method make this possible.

title: In silico cyclic-minipeptides predicting antibody-free early-diagnosis of Ebola virus
abstract: In this work, in silico cyclic-minipeptide candidates were computationally generated aiming to develop antibody-free sandwichbased early-diagnosis of ebola virus (EBOV). Presently there are few approved early-rapid EBOV diagnosis, despite many antibody-based efforts. Cyclic-minipeptides were chosen here because i) their vast sequence numbers facilitate designs fitting the diagnostic sensibility and specificity requirements, ii) they are easy and cheaper to scale-up for production, and iii) their rigidity could be more resistant to denaturing-buffers for EBOV early disinfection during assay.

title: What Can the Records of Published Self-Driving Laboratories Predict About a New Platform? A Step-Level Database and Explorer
abstract: Published closed-loop self-driving laboratories (SDLs) are described in prose, so what their records could predict about a new platform has not been tested. I release sdl-workflows , a database of 237 SDL papers coded by a language model as ordered steps, each with an operation and the type of module performing it, and as connections between modules, each with a transfer mode such as fixed tubing, a robot arm or a person (2610 steps and 1681 connections). On 30 held-out papers, the records agreed with an independent coding by a second model (micro-F1 0.891 to 0.905).

title: The CPOSS Database of Computed Crystal Structures
abstract: Molecular crystal structure prediction (CSP) has radically evolved over the last two decades from a niche research topic to a tool for solid form prediction and derisking. The Control and Prediction of the Organic Solid State (CPOSS) project led by Professor Sarah (Sally) Price has developed CSP over more than two decades of research, generating a large number of deeply researched landscapes, populated by alternative crystal packings for a given chemical system, including structures and systems that have not been observed experimentally.

title: CoO Nanoislands as Metal Oxide Precursors for Surface-Supported Co–BDA Coordination Networks
abstract: Metal oxide nanoislands offer a localized source of metal centers for the on-surface assembly of coordination networks. Here, we investigate the adsorption and thermal evolution of 4,4'-biphenyldicarboxylic acid (BDA) on CoO nanoislands supported on Au(111) under ultrahigh vacuum using infrared reflection absorption spectroscopy (IRAS), scanning tunneling microscopy (STM), and density functional theory (DFT). At 400 K, BDA forms two coexisting populations: carboxylate species anchored to CoO and a predominantly flat-lying, hydrogen-bonded molecular layer on Au(111).

title: From Execution to Discovery : Physical Verification as the Key Gap in AI Agents for Science
abstract: Why can AI agents operate reliably in digital environments such as software development yet still struggle to achieve autonomous scientific discovery? We argue that this gap reflects not only limitations in model capability but also differences in how agent capabilities are externalized and how reliably environments can verify the consequences of agent actions.

title: Donor-level validation of Raman spectroscopy for breast cancer subtype classification
How Chemical Evidence Shapes Mechanistic Reasoning and Prediction by Large Language Models: Fine-Grained Inference in Nucleoside-Derived Supramolecular Gelation
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) offer a distinctive capability for chemical problem solving by integrating chemical knowledge and experimental evidence through reasoning expressed in language. Yet how chemical evidence reshapes their predictions and expressed rationales is not self-evident and has received limited examination, particularly for challenging chemical problems. Here, using nucleoside-derived supramolecular gelation as a testbed, we systematically varied the evidence provided to LLMs and quantitatively evaluated their predictions and the mechanistic alignment of generated rationales.

title: Clusteroluminescence-enabled active optical waveguiding in polyesters
abstract: Organic active waveguides are emerging as multifunctional photonic materials capable of simultaneously transmitting light and regulating optical signals through wavelength conversion and emission modulation. However, most reported systems rely on high-quality single crystals, doped matrices, or complex fabrication procedures, limiting their scalability and practical implementation.

title: Multifaceted Control of Triplet-Pair Spin Dynamics in Intramolecular Singlet Fission at Room Temperature
abstract: The spin evolution dynamics of the correlated triplet pair (TT) decide the fate of the number of triplet (T1) excitons after photoexcitation in singlet fission (SF) materials, yet accurately resolving its relaxation pathways remains elusive. In this work, we systematically elucidate the spin dynamics of intramolecular SF in covalently linked TIPS-pentacene dimers with different inter-triplet exchange coupling (J) values and their dynamic fluctuations by externally perturbing the total spin Hamiltonian via the solventmediated external heavy-atom effect and the magnetic field effect.

title: Unraveling Two Nonlinear Rheological Peaks in Filled Rubber: Chain-Arm Retraction and Bound-Rubber Dynamics
abstract: Carbon-black-filled nitrile butadiene rubber (NBR) exhibits two maxima in its nonlinear oscillatory response, quantified here by a Fourier-based Nonlinearity Index (NLI). The higher-strain Peak I is inherited from the neat long-chain-branched matrix, whereas the lower-strain Peak II appears only after filler addition and is markedly more sensitive to carbon-black grade. We use a molecular description that separates the intrinsic dynamics of the matrix from those of the dynamically active boundrubber population.

title: Supramolecular Control of Photoswitching in a Chiral Azobenzene
abstract: The photochemical behaviour of azobenzene photoswitches is strongly influenced by molecular structure and the surrounding chemical environment, while supramolecular interactions offer an additional means of modulating their switching response. We report the synthesis and photoswitching behaviour of chiral azobenzene derivatives incorporating a BINOL framework and thiourea hydrogen-bonding groups. The thiourea-containing photoswitch 1 undergoes reversible E→Z and Z→E photoisomerization while retaining its chiroptical response.

title: Evaluating the Dimensionality of Molecular Ensembles Using Deep Neural Network Stochastic Autoencoders
abstract: Stochastic autoencoders (SAEs), which omit the Kullback–Leibler prior-matching term of variational autoencoders and are therefore suited to reconstruction rather than generative sampling, offer a nonlinear route to reducing the dimensionality of molecular ensembles, but their behavior across systems of differing size and flexibility is poorly characterized. Training SAEs on molecular dynamics trajectories of oxycodone, deca-alanine, crambin, a bromodomain–JQ1 complex, and HIV-1 protease, we find that reconstruction error plateaus at a system- and model-dependent latent dimensionality, that…

title: Fourier Transform Method for Surface Area Burial
abstract: We develop a method that uses the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to efficiently calculate changes in the solvent accessible surface area (SASA) at many relative translations of two binding partners. For each binding partner, the buried surface area (BSA) is computed using the cross-correlation of a grid-based discretization of its SASA and of a solvent exclusion grid from its binding partner. This approach improves the tractability of exhaustive interface burial calculations by reducing computational complexity, making it particularly valuable for analyzing large biomolecular systems.

title: Automated Static and Dynamic Contact-Angle Analysis with Machine Learning
abstract: We present an autonomous machine-learning model, Conan-MLII, for fast, reproducible contact-angle measurement. The model was trained on >32 million synthetic images generated from Young–Laplace solutions spanning θ = 20◦–180◦, including the effects of gravity, multiple image scales and surface perturbations (roughness, reflection) as well as including sampling offsets to provide contact-point invariance. An improved contact-point identification (CPID) routine is integrated to enable autonomous processing of real images.

title: Examining Copper Lead Surface Alloys as Potential Catalysts for the Electrochemical Carbon Dioxide Reduction
abstract: The conversion of carbon dioxide into useful or environmentally benign chemicals is currently of great interest to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Yet in spite of numerous efforts effective CO2 conversion still presents a considerable challenge. One of the most promising catalysts for CO2 conversion to hydrocarbons is copper. In this computational study based on density functional theory we have addressed bimetallic PbCu catalysts to elucidate whether there are synergistic catalytic effects through the alloying of Cu with Pb, as suggested experimentally.

title: Ensemble Molecular Surface Electrostatic Potential Descriptors as Informative Features for Active Learning
abstract: Active learning ideally needs informative and inexpensive features that provide reliable uncertainty estimates. General interaction properties function (GIPF) descriptors, which encode molecular surface electrostatic potential, are informative but usually computed by density functional approximations on individual structures, which is not only costly but also neglects conformational flexibility. In this work, we compute GIPF descriptors efficiently based on force-field point charges over conformer ensembles via an automated pipeline starting from SMILES strings.

title: Conserved recognition and divergent peripheral dynamics of designed statin analogues at human HMG-CoA reductase: ensemble docking and replicated molecular dynamics
abstract: Human 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl coenzyme A reductase (HMGCR) recognizes statins through a conserved polar binding region, while peripheral chemical differences may alter protein–ligand dynamics. We docked 13 chemically defined statin-related molecular states across six ligand-bound HMGCR crystal structures using three independent searches per state–receptor combination (234 searches). Eight selected states were then evaluated in three independently seeded 50 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations each (24 trajectories; 1.2 μs total).

title: Regio- and Stereoselective Transition Metal-Catalyzed Hydrometallation of SF 5 -alkynes with Group 14 Metalloids (Si, Ge, Sn)
abstract: Hydrometallation of polarized alkynes is a powerful technique to access regio- and stereocontrolled vinyl-metal intermediates. The pentafluorosulfanyl (SF 5 ) group, often called "super-CF 3 ", offers a promising, non-PFAS alternative to CF 3 chemistry, combining enhanced electron-withdrawing properties with remarkable stability. While hydrofunctionalization of SF 5 -alkynes has so far been limited to the β-carbon, we report the first regioselective hydrometallation at the α-carbon of SF 5 -alkynes.

title: Stereodivergent Organocatalytic Glycosylation of 2-Deoxyglycosides
abstract: The stereocontrolled construction of glycosidic linkages from 2-deoxyglycoside donors remains a major challenge in the synthesis of complex oligosaccharides. Herein, we report catalyst-controlled glycosylation protocols that deliver either anomer on demand from the same glycosyl donor, across a broad range of acceptors through simple variation of the chiral Brønsted acid catalyst. Systematic evaluation of a library of readily accessible chiral Brønsted acids reveals how catalyst, donor, and acceptor jointly govern reactivity and stereoselectivity.

title: Copper-Catalyzed Defluorinative Coupling of gem-Difluoroallenes with Grignard Reagents
abstract: gem-Difluoroallenes undergo copper-catalyzed defluorinative coupling with alkyl and aryl Grignard reagents to give monofluoroallenes. Using Cu(OAc)2 (10 mol%) in THF at −20 °C, eleven products are obtained in 64–95% isolated yield. The transformation replaces one fluorine atom while retaining the cumulated diene. Catalyst screening and substrate scope are described, together with a tentative carbocupration/β-fluoride-elimination pathway.

title: Performance and Design Limits of Membraneless Flow Electrochemical Cells: A Combined Secondary Current and Multiphase Flow Analysis
abstract: The membraneless electrolyzer concept has recently gained significant attention as an alternative electrolyzer design which is potentially more durable, flexible, and inexpensive due to the absence of any fragile membrane or diaphragm. While different conceptual designs have been put forward so far, the literature lacks clear quantitative insights on key design and performance parameters. This work presents a comprehensive analysis of the membraneless design encompassing all the primary design concepts i.e. flow-by and flow-through.

title: Collection Effects Behind Genomic-DNA SERS Classification
Silicon‑Noded Cross-Ligation Platform Enabled by Customizable and Moisture-Stable Bis(polyfluoroalkoxy)silanes
abstract: Connecting modules to central nodes is a powerful assembly strategy, as exemplified by DNA/RNA, MOFs, and SuFEx/PFEx chemistry. However, SuFEx and PFEx are largely confined to amine- and phenol-type modules and the alcohol modules could be problematic for SuFEx due to potential dehydroxylative reactions. Silicon‑noded cross-ligation offers an attractive alternative because both alcohols and phenols can serve as reliable modules to form stable silyl ethers, but lacks programmable stepwise ligation hubs comparable to those in SuFEx/PFEx.

title: Thermodynamically informed and balance-preserving neural networks for direct vapor–liquid flash calculations
abstract: Pressure-temperature vapor-liquid equilibrium (PT-VLE) flash calculations are performed repeatedly in compositional-flow simulations and can dominate runtime. To reduce this cost, we propose three thermodynamically informed GibbsFlashNN models that directly predict phase state, compositions, and vapor fraction. A common allocation decoder algebraically enforces nonnegativity, composition normalization, and component-wise material balance.

title: Ligand-Enabled C–CF3 coupling at tetracoordinated Au(III)
abstract: The formation of C–CF3 bonds is an important challenge in organofluorine chemistry. Understanding the factors governing this process is key to develop new synthetic strategies. Here, we report ligand-enabled C–CF3 coupling at tetracoordinate Au(III) centres supported by hemilabile P^N ligands. A series of well-defined Au(III) trifluoromethyl complexes bearing aryl, vinyl or alkynyl groups were prepared and shown to undergo thermal reductive elimination, affording the corresponding C–CF3 coupling products in high yields (86% on average of 17 examples).

title: A respiratory microdomain links ubiquinone biosynthesis to succinate dehydrogenase in an apicomplexan mitochondrion lacking Complex I
abstract: Mitochondrial complex I (CI) is a major entry point for NADH-derived electrons and an important site of redox regulation in most eukaryotes. However, apicomplexan parasites, including Toxoplasma gondii, lack CI, raising a fundamental question of how mitochondrial respiration is organized in these parasites. Here, we identify a parasite-specific mitochondrial microdomain that physically and functionally couples ubiquinone (UQ) biosynthesis to succinate dehydrogenase (SDH).

title: Toxicological effects of acetyl tributyl citrate exposure on the progression of uterine fibroids and cervical cancer
abstract: BackgroundUterine fibroids (UFs) and cervical cancer (CC) are two common gynecological tumors, the pathogenesis of which has not yet been fully elucidated, with environmental factors playing a significant role. Acetyl tributyl citrate (ATBC), a widely used plasticizer, has been proven to pose a threat to human health. Although studies have indicated that ATBC exposure may be associated with tumorigenesis, the specific roles and molecular mechanisms of ATBC in UFs and CC remain unclear.ObjectiveThis study aims to investigate the molecular mechanisms of ATBC-related UFs and CC using network toxicology, machine learning, and multidimensional bioinformatics approaches.MethodsNetwork toxicology methods were used to identify the relevant targets of ATBC, UFs, and CC. Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes enrichment analysis were employed to explore the potential target gene pathways of ATBC-related UFs and CC. Transcriptomics analysis, Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator, and Support Vector Machine - Recursive Feature Elimination algorithms were used to determine the core targets of ATBC-related UFs and CC, and the discrimination of core genes among them was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic curve. Immune infiltration analysis was used to analyze the relationship between the expression of core target genes and the infiltration levels of various immune cells, while molecular docking and in vitro cell experiments were used to validate the above results.ResultsWe identified 12 targets related to UFs and 153 targets related to CC, of which 11 were common targets for UFs and CC, significantly enriched in the ERBB signaling pathway and oxidative stress response pathway. F10, ABCB1, MMP9, CDK2, PIK3CA, and GABRA2 were identified as the core targets of ATBC-related UFs, while CDK2 and DHFR were identified as the core targets of ATBC-related CC. Among them, CDK2 is a cross-disease hub target for UFs and CC. In UFs tissues (MMP9, GABRA2, and CDK2) and CC tissues (CDK2 and DHFR), the expression of these genes was significantly higher than that in normal tissues. These genes were significantly associated with immune cell infiltration. Molecular docking and in vitro cell experiments results confirmed the stable interactions between ATBC and these targets.ConclusionThis study reveals that some key targets play important roles in the relationship between ATBC and UFs and CC, providing new insights into the mechanisms of ATBC in gynecological tumors and offering potential targets for future prevention and treatment strategies.

title: Effects Of Lymphocyte Trafficking on Antiretroviral Drug Distribution within the Lymph Node
abstract: The lymph node (LN) lobule is physically isolated by selective transport barriers, including high endothelial venules and sinusoidal endothelium, that restrict free diffusion of many antiretroviral (ARV) drugs used to treat HIV, especially non-lipophilic compounds. Recent spatial pharmacokinetic analyses have suggested that passive diffusion alone cannot explain observed ARV concentrations in lymphoid tissues, raising the possibility that lymphocytes may act as incidental drug carriers.

title: Discovery of P1-P2 depeptidized boronic acid based Plasmodium falciparum SUB1 inhibitor
abstract: The Plasmodium falciparum subtilisin-like serine protease 1 (PfSUB1) is an essential enzyme required for parasite egress from host red blood cells and represents a promising target for antimalarial drugs. Peptidic boronic acids are potent reported PfSUB1 inhibitors, however their drug-likeness is limited by their pronounced peptidic character. Based on molecular docking studies using peptidic boronic acids, we designed a series of partially depeptidized PfSUB1 inhibitors by replacing the P1-P2 dipeptide fragment with a 3-aminomethylphenylboronic acid core. Structure-activity relationship (SAR) investigations targeting interaction with active-site residue Lys138 revealed that introducing a meta-carboxylate group (compound 3a) markedly enhanced inhibitory activity, yielding a low-nanomolar PfSUB1 inhibitor (IC50= 10.2 nM). Bioisosteric replacement of the carboxylic acid demonstrated that an N-acylsulfonamide group (compound 4k) retained high enzymatic potency (IC50= 13.5 nM)). In cellular assays against blood-stage P. falciparum (3D7 strain), the leading depeptidized boronic acids exhibited growth inhibition with values in the low-micromolar range suggesting that further structural modifications are needed to enhance membrane permeability across host and parasite membranes to reach exonemes prior to egress. Overall, this study validates the P1-P2 depeptidization of boronic acid scaffolds and provides key SAR insights for the rational design of non-peptidic PfSUB1-targeted antimalarials.

title: Distortion states as robust embeddings for quantifying and forecasting atomistic damage from electron microscopy
abstract: Distortion states as robust embeddings for quantifying and forecasting atomistic damage from electron microscopy

title: Toward a Quantum Information Foundation for Neutron Scattering
abstract: Neutron scattering is a central probe of quantum materials, yet what quantum information can, in principle, be extracted from a scattering experiment remains unclear. Here we formulate neutron scattering as a quantum measurement, with the scattering amplitudes acting as Kraus operators on the material state. This provides a unified description of conventional intensity, coherent scattering, interferometric measurements, and entanglement witnesses, including those based on quantum Fisher information. We then ask how far this connection can be extended to nonlinear properties of a quantum state. For two independently prepared samples, we derive the general structure of probe-mediated measurement probabilities and show that, for spin-projection-conserving dynamics, low-order scattering cannot resolve certain many-body coherences required to determine purity. Conversely, an idealized single-spin protocol shows how probe-mediated exchange can access purity when the appropriate two-copy operation is realized. Our results establish a quantum-information description of neutron scattering and delineate the information accessible through conventional and interferometric measurements.

title: Quasicrystals are Functionally Graded Materials
abstract: Quasicrystals exhibit long-range order without translational periodicity, posing challenges to compute their electronic properties. Here we show that a quasicrystal can be represented exactly as a periodic approximant with a spatially graded phason, establishing a connection to functionally graded materials. Building on this connection, we develop a controlled quantum theory of quasicrystals. We derive a state-dependent control parameter governed by the quantum metric of local Bloch states, determining when finite approximations are reliable. We further construct a Hamiltonian that correctly predicts Bragg gap positions, quasimomentum equivalence, and quasiperiodic eigenstates to all orders in phason strain within a finite Fourier window. We verify the theory numerically and propose a diffraction-based experimental test of the gap shift induced by phason strain. Our framework opens a route to predicting the electronic structure and functional properties of quasicrystals using methods developed for functionally graded materials.

title: The Oxygen Artifact in Visible-Light-Driven CO2 Reduction Catalyzed by Molecular Catalysts
abstract: Visible-light-driven CO2 reduction using homogeneous molecular systems has attracted considerable attention as a strategy for converting greenhouse gases into value-added fuels. In this study, we investigated the influence of oxygen on a representative photocatalytic system composed of an iron porphyrin catalyst, a photosensitizer, triethylamine (TEA) as a sacrificial electron donor, and trifluoroethanol (TFE) as a proton donor.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Charge-Transfer Engineering Controls Excited-State Dynamics and Supramolecular Assembly in Luminescent Au(I) Complexes
abstract: Coupling excited-state control with supramolecular self-assembly within a single molecular design remains a central challenge in luminescent materials chemistry. Here, we explore charge-transfer (CT) engineering as a strategy to address both features in a family of luminescent Au(I) bisphosphine complexes. Homoleptic derivatives bearing pyrene, phenanthrene, or triphenylene chromophores were compared with a heteroleptic pyrene/phenanthrene complex designed to promote interchromophoric electronic communication. The homoleptic complexes display predominantly room-temperature fluorescence, with increasing phosphorescence contributions associated with progressive metal perturbation of the excited states. In the heteroleptic complex, the combination of electronically differentiated chromophores enables access to a T2-mediated pathway that promotes room-temperature pyrene phosphorescence, as supported by solvent-dependent photophysical measurements and theoretical calculations. Addition of [Au(CN)2]− enhances fluorescence in all cases, with a 6-fold increase for the heteroleptic complex, and promotes its organization into extended luminescent wires driven by a combination of C–H···N≡C hydrogen bonding and π···π stacking interactions. These results show how chromophore differentiation within an Au(I) coordination scaffold can couple excited-state modulation with supramolecular organization, providing a design strategy for responsive luminescent assemblies.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Controlling Polymorphism and Particle Size in Zr-Based Metal-Organic Frameworks Through Preformed Nodes and Machine-Learning-Assisted Synthesis
abstract: Framework topology and particle size jointly govern pore architecture, diffusion limitations, and accessible surface area, making their simultaneous control essential for functional metal-organic framework (MOF) design. Achieving reproducible control over both remains a central challenge in MOF chemistry, particularly for systems capable of crystallizing in multiple polymorphs. Here, we systematically explore the synthesis of two Zr-based MOFs, NU-1000 and NU-901, which share the same Zr6-oxo cluster and pyrene-tetrabenzoate linker but differ in topology. To remove variability arising from in situ precursor formation, we employed preformed Zr6-oxo clusters as well-defined nodes. Building on this controlled starting point, multiple particle-size regimes (<100 nm to ∼1 µm) were accessed through systematic variation of modulator identity and loading, co-modulator content, linker equivalents, temperature, and dilution. Machine-learning (ML) analysis quantitatively disentangles the multivariate influences governing phase selection and particle-size evolution. This integrated approach enables predictive navigation of the synthesis parameter space, providing reproducible access to MOFs with defined size regimes and controlled topology. Together, these results establish a generalizable experimental-computational workflow that transforms empirical MOF synthesis into a predictable, designable process, enabling rational control over polymorphism and growth in structurally adaptable framework materials.

title: Comets may not have kick-started life on Earth after all
abstract: Simulations suggest that few cometary impacts could have delivered enough hydrogen cyanide to support the chemistry that preceded life

title: Benchmarking Machine Learning Models for Viral Nanobody Epitope Prediction
abstract: Rapid development of therapeutics against emerging viral pathogens increasingly depends on machine learning (ML), both to generate candidate binders and for structural validation. Nanobodies (Nbs), or single-domain antibodies, are promising antiviral therapeutics, but accurate in silico prediction of viral epitopes remains challenging. Here we benchmark three ML-based structure prediction models, Boltz-2, Chai-1 and AlphaFold3 (AF3), against a curated data set of viral antigen-nanobody complexes deposited after the AF3 training cutoff. AF3 outperformed the other models: success (interface DockQ > 0.23) rose from 33% with a single seed to 50% and 65% with 10 and 100 seeds-per-target, respectively, compared with 18% for Boltz-2 and 30% for Chai-1. Using an expanded data set, we evaluated confidence metrics and found that a strict ipTM cutoff of 0.8, or a combination of ipTM ≥ 0.6 with a CDR3 loop pLDDT ≥ 60, reliably excluded incorrect predictions while retaining most successful ones. We further establish best practices for two AF3-specific capabilities, the choice of antigen multimeric state and the inclusion of N-glycosylation, both of which can be decisive for epitope success depending on the target. Finally, we apply these guidelines to two design problems: ranking a library of VEEV-neutralizing nanobodies and mapping the epitope of the broadly neutralizing nanobody CC3 across homologous alphavirus antigens. These results provide a practical framework for ML-based viral nanobody epitope prediction and design.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Development and cross-cohort evaluation of a multimodal deep-learning model for ER, PR and HER2 status classification in breast cancer
abstract: Background: Estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR) and HER2 status guide systemic treatment in breast cancer. Multimodal models are rarely benchmarked against key biomarker molecular baselines or evaluated for cross-cohort calibration. We assessed incremental value, dependence on label-proximal HER2 transcripts, and transport of discrimination and calibration. Methods. A model combining whole-slide images, transcriptomes, age and stage was developed in TCGA-BRCA (1051 patients; ER/PR/HER2 analysis sets: 1001/998/1006) and evaluated in CPTAC-BRCA (120 patients; 118/113/95).

title: Influence of antibody-antigen interaction on fluorescence of Rhodamine 6G conjugated to the antibodies measured in human serum
abstract: Fluorescent dyes conjugated to monoclonal antibodies specifically trastuzumab (TRAS) and pertuzumab (PERT) serve as sensitive reporters of changes in the local energetic environment arising from antibody-antibody and antibody-antigen interactions. Upon covalent conjugation, the antibody local environment perturbates the energetic state of the dye, resulting in changes of the fluorescence emission energy and emission width of the dye. The dependence of these spectral parameters on antibody concentration was measured in HBS-8, diluted and undiluted human serum. In addition, the emission energy and emission width of dye-conjugated TRAS were investigated as a function of recombinant human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) extracellular domain concentration in HBS-8 and in diluted and undiluted human serum. Antibody-antibody and antibody-antigen interactions produce remarkable contributions into the emission energy and emission width. These contributions depend on the composition of the surrounding medium. Our study showed that the samples containing 100 nM TRAS in serum exhibited the largest spectral changes upon interaction with HER2 suggesting that antibody-antigen interaction are not linear across concentration range of the antibodies. Moreover, our results demonstrate that interactions between dye-conjugated antibodies and their binding partners can be detected under physiologically relevant conditions. These findings establish fluorescence emission energy and emission width analysis as a potential approach for probing antibody interactions in complex biological matrices.

title: Combining Relevant Expert Knowledge Using Mixtures of Feedback Fuzzy Cognitive Maps
abstract: A neuro-symbolic system should combine only relevant answers from expert agents or other knowledge sources. Using only relevant experts for a given input query becomes ever more important for accuracy and scalability as the knowledge network grows and connects ever more knowledge sources. We extend the standard definition of relevance from the legal theory of evidence: An answer is relevant if and only if it is both probative and material for the matter at hand given the knowledge available. We apply this relevancy scheme to mixing the feedback fuzzy cognitive maps (FCMs) of real or artificial experts. The expert FCM directed causal graphs mix or combine into a common knowledge network. We compare the equilibrium limit-cycle predictions or answers of the experts to the answers of the mixture FCM and then estimate the probative status of answers by their difference or variation. A new Bayes-like theorem de-mixes the knowledge mixture into corresponding posterior-like FCMs that also allow relevancy-based comparisons. The result is a final set of relevancy mixing weights that produces a relevancy-mixed FCM knowledge network for the given query. So different queries produce different relevancy-mixed FCMs. We demonstrate this relevancy approach using generated synthetic FCMs from an actual 13-node expert FCM that models the causes and feedbacks of ischemic-stroke risk.

title: Low cross-plane thermal conductivity of $κ$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ thin films
abstract: The thermal conductivities of (001) $κ$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ thin films deposited on $c$-plane sapphire substrates were measured with frequency-domain thermoreflectance (FDTR). The thermal conductivity increases from 1.83 $^{+0.19}_{-0.18}$ W/m$\cdot$K to 2.26 $^{+0.35}_{-0.40}$ W/m$\cdot$K as the thicknesses increase from 159 nm to 689 nm. This weak thickness dependence indicates that the majority of the intrinsic phonon mean free paths are smaller than the range of investigated film thicknesses. First-principles-based calculations that include phonon-phonon and phonon-boundary scattering capture this size-dependent behavior and support our experimental observation. Temperature-dependent measurements of a 689 nm film from 293 to 400 K show a decrease in thermal conductivity with increasing temperature due to enhanced phonon-phonon scattering. A weaker temperature dependence is observed in a 159 nm film where phonon-boundary scattering becomes more prominent. At comparable film thicknesses, our measured $κ$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ films exhibit lower values of cross-plane thermal conductivity than the other experimentally measured Ga$_2$O$_3$ polymorphs. Our experimental observations are supported by prior predictions, which suggest that the low thermal conductivity of $κ$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ results from its complex crystal structure, which leads to increased anharmonicity and lower phonon group velocities relative to other polymorphs. Thermal management strategies, such as integration with high-thermal-conductivity substrates, may thus be required to mitigate self-heating for $κ$-Ga$_2$O$_3$-based electronic devices.

title: DefectSkills: Guiding AI agents through first-principles calculations for point defects in semiconductors and insulators
abstract: First-principles defect calculations can now be performed autonomously by AI agents, enabled by established computational methods and open-source Python toolkits. However, reliable and repeatable defect calculations require clear scientific and technical guidance that helps agents resolve ambiguities and avoid errors in calculation setup, execution, postprocessing, and analysis. Here, we present DefectSkills, a set of structured prompts that provides human-in-the-loop guidance to AI agents performing first-principles calculations of point defects in semiconductors and insulators using the Vienna Ab initio Simulation Package (VASP). The prompts encode human expertise and guide agents through unit-cell relaxation, electronic-structure and dielectric calculations, phase-stability and chemical-potential analysis, charged-defect supercell generation and calculations, finite-size corrections, formation-energy calculations and thermodynamic analysis, and data backup. By packaging this expertise as reusable agent skills, DefectSkills supports consistent workflow execution across agentic AI systems and reproducible defect calculations.

title: Medial Model of Elastic Curve Contacts, from Clasps to Knits
abstract: Materials constructed from interlocking and tangled fibers are challenging to model and understand due in part to the complex interplay between fiber shape and contact mechanics. Much of our intuition about contact mechanics comes from the Hertzian description, which is based on interactions between convex bodies. However, fibers often form clasp shapes, which involve saddle-shaped contact surfaces; the ability for two interacting bodies to conform to each other along a saddle surface confounds many existing mechanical contact models. Following an observation that contact surfaces between fibers tend to look like minimal, constant mean-curvature surfaces, we seek to test this hypothesis and provide a direct link to geometric modeling methods. To do this, we leverage the medial axis transformation, which generalizes the notion of a Voronoi tessellation to generating curves and surfaces. Through computational studies on an orthogonal clasp and a simple knit structure, we find that the medial axis transformation provides a reasonable model for contact surfaces between identical curves. We also show that a generalization of the medial axis transformation based on radical Voronoi tessellations can be used to well-approximate contact surfaces between non-identical curves. We apply this ``radical axis transform'' to curves of different radii and demonstrate a trend for surfaces to adopt finite mean curvature. Our results may point the way towards more sophisticated geometric methods for modeling tangles.

title: Exact Mirror-Parity Selection Rule for Electron-Phonon Coupling in Two-Dimensional Crystals
abstract: The electron--phonon (e-ph) interaction underlies conventional superconductivity and plays a central role in transport and other many-body phenomena in solids. Here, we derive a symmetry selection rule for e-ph scattering in two-dimensional crystals possessing a horizontal mirror plane, $σ_h$. For electronic states of mirror parity $s_n(\mathbf{k})$ and $s_m(\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{q})$, and a phonon mode of parity $χ_ν(\mathbf{q})$, we show that the e-ph matrix element $g_{mn,ν}(\mathbf{k},\mathbf{q})$ vanishes identically unless $s_n(\mathbf{k})\,χ_ν(\mathbf{q})\, s_m(\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{q})=+1$. The rule follows from the covariance of the phonon-induced deformation potential under $σ_h$, constitutes the $C_s$ case of the general group-theoretical selection rule for matrix elements, and partitions the e-ph interaction throughout the Brillouin zone into symmetry-allowed and symmetry-forbidden scattering channels. Consequently, mirror-even phonons couple electronic states of the same mirror parity, either even--even or odd--odd, whereas mirror-odd phonons couple only states of opposite mirror parity, for both intra- and interband processes. We illustrate the selection rule through first-principles calculations for the two-dimensional superconductor $\mathrm{Sc_2BCH_4}$, where mirror parity is well defined throughout the entire Brillouin zone and symmetry-forbidden matrix elements vanish up to numerical precision. We then extend the analysis to bulk $\mathrm{MgB_2}$, where the rule applies exactly only on mirror-invariant planes of the three-dimensional Brillouin zone. Moving away from these planes removes the exact mirror constraint and activates scattering channels that are symmetry forbidden when the mirror eigenvalues are well defined. Our results establish horizontal mirror symmetry as an exact and practical filter of e-ph scattering processes.

title: OdorSpaces: Visual-Olfactory Embodied Navigation in 3D Environments
abstract: Olfaction provides critical information about airborne chemical cues, yet it remains largely underexplored in embodied AI, with limited prior machine olfaction work focusing primarily on semantic odor perception. We introduce OdorSpaces, a physics-based simulation platform and benchmark for visual-olfactory embodied navigation. OdorSpaces augments Habitat-Sim with 3D odor transport and dispersion simulated by Fire Dynamics Simulator (FDS), enabling agents to navigate photorealistic indoor environments using both visual and olfactory observations. The benchmark includes two representative source-seeking scenarios: invisible gas-leak localization and early-stage fire localization. We develop an initial multimodal reinforcement learning policy that integrates visual observations and olfactory measurements over time. Experiments show that the policy outperforms a diverse set of baselines, establishing a strong reference for future research on visual-olfactory embodied navigation.

title: Shock-driven Jetting at HMX Crystal Surface Asperities
abstract: Shock-induced jetting and recompression are plausible mechanisms for hot spot formation in energetic materials, but remain poorly understood. To this end, we apply all-atom nonreactive molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of a shock-loaded sinusoidal surface asperity in the crystalline explosive HMX (octahydro-1,3,5,7-tetranitro-1,3,5,7-tetrazocine) to quantify the roles of shock strength, asperity geometry, system size, and crystallographic orientation in determining the jetting response. Our simulations span a shock pressure interval of $\approx$4-47 GPa, which captures responses in both detonation initiation and steady-state detonation regimes. We find that shock strength and asperity curvature exert strong influence on jet velocity, temperature, and morphology, while feature size and crystallographic orientation play more modest roles. Jet morphology correlates strongly with the HMX ambient-pressure phase diagram and the narrow temperature range associated with its liquid phase. Coherent jets form when focusing and dissipation are sufficient to drive local temperatures above the melting point, while formation of molecular plumes is seemingly connected to jet temperatures exceeding the liquid-vapor transition temperature. Formation of plumes is unlike the jetting responses seen in metals, which typically exhibit liquid phases that are stable over wider temperature intervals. This work proposes a simple hypothesis for the connection between jet morphology and ambient-pressure phase diagrams that can be readily tested in other explosives and metals. It also provides a foundation for ongoing nonreactive and reactive MD simulations of jet impact and recompression to quantify the role played by jets in forming hot spots in HMX-based explosives.

title: Tractography-Based Insights into Neuroplasticity and Clinical Heterogeneity in Parkinson's Disease Subtypes.
abstract: Parkinson's disease shows substantial heterogeneity across motor, cognitive, and non-motor domains, reflecting variable patterns of neurodegeneration and compensation across distributed brain circuits. Diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (dMRI) tractography enables pathway-specific characterization of white-matter alterations and provides a framework for linking clinical subtypes to tract-level patterns that may be obscured by skeleton-based or connectomic averaging.
venue: The Neuroscientist : a review journal bringing neurobiology, neurology and psychiatry

title: Obituary: Walter E. Mader Jr.
Spin-Density-Driven Hybrid Spin Splitting in Collinear Compensated Magnets
abstract: Nonrelativistic spin splitting in collinear compensated magnets is constrained by spin-group symmetry, with distinct alternating and Zeeman-type splitting typically associated with altermagnets and fully compensated ferrimagnets, respectively. From a spin-density perspective, we propose a class of hybrid compensated magnets in which alternating-like and Zeeman-type spin splitting coexist within a single collinear compensated state. Using a minimal two-sector model, we demonstrate that this coexistence arises from competition between directional sublattice dispersion and the sector-dependent energy biases arising from the same structural inequivalence. First-principles calculations provide a proof of concept in a crossed bilayer of unequal-width Janus graphene nanoribbons, where the structurally inequivalent ribbons retain approximately symmetry-related spin-density distributions. The valence and conduction sectors support direction-selective spin transport and energy-selective spin-polarized states, respectively. These results connect the spatial organization of spin density with the electronic response to structural inequivalence, providing a design principle for hybrid spin splitting in compensated magnets.

title: Spin-orbit-locked symmetry and the stability of the triangular Dirac spin liquid in the ytterbium delafossites
abstract: The Yb delafossites NaYbSe$_2$, KYbSe$_2$, CsYbSe$_2$ and NaYbO$_2$ are candidates for the triangular U(1) Dirac spin liquid, QED$_3$ with $N_f=4$, but their exchange is spin-orbit coupled. Under their spin-orbit-locked space group we determine which operators the XXZ anisotropy and the bond-dependent couplings $J_{\pm\pm}$, $J_{z\pm}$ induce, and at what order. Symmetry forbids every Dirac mass, density and current at any order and, assuming adiabatic continuity, any new monopole term through charge three. At linear order the couplings reach only spin-2 members of the quartic multiplets $\mathbf{20}'$ and $\mathbf{84}$, which share their dimensions with Heisenberg-allowed operators. At second order $J_{\pm\pm}$ and $J_{z\pm}$ renormalize the anisotropy through $J_{z\pm}^2-2J_{\pm\pm}^2$, and nine spin-1 quartics without Heisenberg partners appear, irrelevant at $O(1/N)$. A single layer of a stable Heisenberg spin liquid thus acquires no relevant Lorentz-scalar operator from spin-orbit coupling. The Heisenberg liquid itself allows a Lorentz-vector $\mathbf{20}'$ quartic of large-$N$ dimension 2.92, with two-loop $ε$-expansion estimates 2.9-3.5. Rhombohedral stacking adds triplet-monopole tunneling between layers at first order. At the transition to 120$^\circ$ order the anisotropy is relevant, with crossover exponent $y_T\simeq0.74$-1, and exact diagonalization shows that easy-plane anisotropy selects the chiral-Ising class. The out-of-plane spectrum at the K point then stays gapless, and the spin-flip to non-spin-flip ratio grows as $ω^{-0.56}$ at leading order. Existing KYbSe$_2$ neutron data below $J$ do not fix the K-point exponent. In-plane fields induce a chiral mass and an out-of-plane moment proportional to $\sin3\varphi$, zero along the bonds and canceling between CsYbSe$_2$ layers, which the planar thermal Hall effect can test.

title: Why strong spin-orbit coupling does not destabilize the Dirac spin liquid in the Yb delafossites
abstract: The Yb delafossites NaYbSe$_2$, KYbSe$_2$, CsYbSe$_2$ and NaYbO$_2$ are candidates for the U(1) Dirac spin liquid (DSL) of the triangular lattice. Strong spin-orbit coupling gives their exchange an XXZ anisotropy $Δ$ and bond-dependent couplings $J_{\pm\pm}$, $J_{z\pm}$ that lock the spin frame to the lattice. We show that, within a single layer of a stable Heisenberg DSL, these couplings generate no relevant Lorentz-scalar operator of their own. Inversion at the bond centers removes the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya channel that gaps the kagome DSL, so the locked symmetry forbids a mass, density or current at any order and, assuming continuity, any new monopole term through charge three. Every Lorentz-scalar four-fermion operator induced by spin-orbit coupling shares an SU(4) multiplet, and hence its scaling dimension, with a Heisenberg-allowed one, and the nine non-scalar quartics without such a partner arise only at second order and are irrelevant at large $N$. The Heisenberg DSL itself allows a Lorentz-vector quartic of large-$N$ dimension 2.92, which a stable phase must also render irrelevant. Beyond a single layer, spin-orbit coupling opens an interlayer monopole channel in rhombohedral stacking. If the Heisenberg DSL is instead multicritical, an anisotropy as small as that of KYbSe$_2$ matters only below tens of mK. At the transition to 120$^\circ$ order the anisotropy is relevant, and exact diagonalization indicates that easy-plane anisotropy selects the chiral-Ising class. Existing KYbSe$_2$ neutron data below $J$ do not yet fix the K-point exponent, and gapless out-of-plane spin fluctuations at the K point would test the chiral-Ising selection.

title: An Expert-Augmented Deep Learning Approach for Synthesis Route Evaluation
abstract: Selecting multistep synthetic routes remains a major bottleneck in computer-aided synthesis planning because high-quality negative data are scarce and no single reported route can completely define route quality. We introduce an expert-augmented framework that combines large-scale reference-based route learning with expert-defined chemical feasibility assessment. Large-scale pre-training on literature-derived reference routes yields 60.3% top-1 reference-route recovery on held-out targets.

title: Statistically Robust Characterization of Polaron and Bipolaron Intrinsic Traps in Amorphous Silica Reveals the Role of Network Flexibility in Electron Localisation
abstract: Intrinsic electron localization in amorphous silica (a-SiO2) contributes to charge trapping and defect generation in silica-based electronic materials - a phenomenon that degrades logic-device performance but can be exploited for memory applications. However, the structural distribution of one- and two-electron traps remains incompletely characterized, largely because the disordered covalent network of a-SiO2 spans a vast configurational space. To address this, we perform statistical sampling to select a representative 200-model subset of defect-free bulk a-SiO2 structures from a structurally converged parent set of 2512 models, generated via classical melt-quench molecular dynamics simulations. We then characterize the intrinsic one- and two-electron traps in this subset using HSE06 density functional theory calculations. Analysis of neutral precursor sites shows that trapping propensity is not determined by a universal O-Si-O angle or Si-O bond length; it is controlled by the accessibility of the relaxed trap geometry, requiring both local strain and medium-range network flexibility. Single electrons predominantly form edge-centred polarons on distorted SiO4 tetrahedra, with occupied states 3.1-4.3 eV below the conduction band minimum. Injection of a second electron drives stronger lattice relaxation, most commonly Si-O bond elongation leading to rupture, thereby forming threefold-coordinated-Si (Si3) bipolarons and, in some cases, Si-Si-bonded bipolaron configurations. The calculated bipolaron energy ranges are consistent with optical absorption features at 3.7, 4.7, and 6.4 eV associated with intrinsic electron localization.

title: Hydrogen-induced modification of the local charge density in MnSb$_2$Te$_4$
abstract: We investigate the effects of ionic hydrogen (H$^+$) intake on the occupied and unoccupied states of MnSb$_2$Te$_4$, a van der Waals magnetic material. Using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and time-resolved ARPES, combined with resonant and core level photoemission, we reveal that hydrogen binds near specific lattice sites, locally redistributing charge density and reshaping the valence band spectral weight. While the band gap and picosecond carrier dynamics show only minor changes upon hydrogenation, the conduction band exhibits a striking stoichiometry-dependent response. These findings indicate that hydrogen interacts strongly with the intrinsic defects in the lattice, acting as a selective dopant in MnSb$_2$Te$_4$. Our work provides a spectroscopic basis for using hydrogen as a tool for the control of the electronic and magnetic properties in layered 2D materials.

title: Ablating Design Choices for Protein Ensemble Generators Across Structural Regimes
abstract: Generative models of protein conformational ensembles inherit much of their design from structure prediction for folded proteins. Ordered and disordered proteins, however, occupy distinct structural regimes, and we investigate how design choices hold up across them. Using a minimal C$α$ flow-matching model, we ablate choices of architecture, sequence conditioning, rigid-body alignment and training source, and evaluate each variant against experimental SAXS and NMR chemical-shift data partitioned into ordered, disordered, multi-domain and transitional proteins. Mixture-of-experts routing, a static pair representation and a disorder probe have no detectable effect, a smaller protein language model performs worse on ordered proteins but not on disordered ones, and alignment in the loss degrades agreement with SAXS. Replacing coarse-grained simulations of disordered proteins with fragment-assembled ensembles improves agreement with chemical shifts at a cost to SAXS, while an equal mixture of the two keeps most of the gain at a smaller cost. This points to the training data, rather than the architecture, as the main constraint.

title: Process-zone condensation: a discretization-exact reduced cell model for FE$^2$ analysis of composites with fibre-matrix debonding and matrix plasticity
abstract: Periodic composites with cohesive interfaces and matrix plasticity require nonlinear cell solutions in multiscale analysis. Process-zone condensation eliminates the linear elastic remainder of the cell by a Schur complement, retaining all interfacial and process-zone internal variables. Influence matrices recover macroscopic stress and consistent tangent. One back-substitution per increment checks that the matrix outside the retained zone remains elastic. While this holds, the reduction is exact relative to the full discretisation, also with a plastic matrix, and requires no training. In an E-glass/epoxy cell, eight of nine two-dimensional paths agree with the full cell to 1e-11 in stress and tangent; the check flags the ninth. Three paths on each of two three-dimensional meshes need zone expansion. Excluding setup and checks, two-dimensional path timings show an aggregate speed-up of 3.3; certified three-dimensional zones show none. In adaptive finite element squared (FE$^2$) simulations of a perforated plate, the reduced solver reproduces the full-cell response within solver tolerances, 1.51 times faster for glass/polypropylene and slower for glass/epoxy. Independent Ansys models agree to below 1e-3 in cell stress and about 0.6% in plate reactions, although local damage and plasticity onsets differ. The advantage depends on zone size, active set and adaptation costs.

title: Long-time Brownian dynamics of hard and sticky colloids by geometric projection
abstract: Particle-resolved colloid simulations are often limited by the fastest microscopic time scale retained in the model, which can be many orders of magnitude shorter than the collective process of interest. This is especially restrictive for aggregating colloids, where explicit near-contact potentials force the time integration to resolve the rapid positional relaxation of bonded pairs within narrow attractive wells. Here we introduce an overdamped constraint-based Brownian dynamics method that replaces the time-resolved integration of stiff near-contact forces by a geometric projection step. After each free Brownian update, hard-sphere exclusion, sticky bonds, and hard-wall interactions are enforced by projecting the particle positions onto the constrained configuration set. The method preserves hard-sphere structure and diffusion, recovers the aggregation kinetics of sticky hard spheres, and extends the physical time reached at fixed computational cost by one to two orders of magnitude relative to the explicit-potential simulations tested here. This acceleration makes Brownian-dominated, low-Péclet electrophoretic deposition accessible to particle-scale simulations, revealing a pathway in which the suspension first densifies and only subsequently develops a bonded network. Implemented as a LAMMPS fix, the framework provides a modular route to long-time Brownian simulations of dense constrained colloidal systems.

title: Ferron polariton Hall effect: Deflecting optically rectified polarization with magnetic fields
abstract: Ferrons are elementary excitations of ferroelectric order that can propagate and transport polarization when excited with light. Here, we show theoretically that ferron polaritons exhibit a Hall effect: an applied magnetic field generates polarization transport perpendicular to the propagation direction of a ferron polariton excited by an incident terahertz pulse. We demonstrate this effect for the example of ferroelectric SnTe using first-principles calculations and a microscopic theory of the phonon-polariton current. The direction and magnitude of the transverse polarization transport can be controlled by the polarization of the terahertz pulse and the applied magnetic field. Our results establish a route toward light-controlled directional transport of electric polarization in ferroelectrics.

title: Surrogate Models for Stochastic Al-Cu Phase-Field Solidification
abstract: Phase-field models resolve microstructural evolution during rapid alloy solidification, but their computational cost limits long trajectories, stochastic ensembles, and studies across process conditions. We present a variance-preserving denoising diffusion bridge model (VP-DDBM) for state-conditioned prediction of two-dimensional Al-Cu solidification. Given the current phase, concentration, and prescribed temperature fields, the model predicts the subsequent state and is applied autoregressively. Across two held-out thermal gradients, VP-DDBM produces lower long-horizon errors than deterministic U-Net and SI-ConvNeXt baselines in domain-mean phase, domain-mean Cu concentration, and leading-tip position. It also retains fine dendritic structure over long rollouts, whereas the deterministic U-Net progressively smooths the morphology. VP-DDBM predicts the phase and concentration evolution approximately $73\times$ faster than the phase-field solver, showing potential for faster process-condition screening and ensemble-based microstructure studies.

title: Cryo-EM structures of Cereibacter sphaeroides ferrochelatase reveal an oligomeric state that occludes the substrate-binding site
abstract: Protoporphyrin IX (PPIX) is the last shared intermediate of heme and (bacterio)chlorophyll ((B)Chl) biosynthesis. Insertion of iron into PPIX by the PPIX ferrochelatase (FeCh) PpfC produces heme, whereas magnesium insertion by magnesium chelatase (MgCh) initiates (B)Chl synthesis. Chlorophototrophic organisms must regulate this biosynthetic node to ensure the correct flux of PPIX to each of these crucial tetrapyrrole products, presenting a particularly acute problem for the facultative bacterium Cereibacter (previously Rhodobacter) sphaeroides, which can switch between chemotrophic…

title: Ether Coordination in Ionomers Switches Function with Length Scale in CO2 Electrolysis
abstract: CO2 electrolysis to CO relies on anion-exchange ionomers (AEIs) in two distinct roles, as the membrane and as the catalyst-layer binder, yet the design criteria for the two roles are rarely separated. Here, we demonstrate that side-chain architecture switches function with length scale by comparing AEIs bearing hexamethylene (HTMA) or ether-containing (EOTMA) trimethylammonium spacers in each role. As a membrane, EOTMA immobilizes most of its water, so 56% greater uptake produces no conductivity gain. The EOTMA membrane also admits K+, which accumulates at the cathode and lowers CO selectivity relative to HTMA. As a binder, the same ether groups improve CO2 accessibility and strengthen interfacial hydrogen bonding, promoting *COOH formation and weakening *CO binding, as shown by impedance, sorption, and spectroscopic analyses. Pairing the HTMA membrane with the EOTMA binder on commercial Ag delivers a CO partial current density of 550.3 mA cm–2 at 3.51 V and 60 °C. Role-optimized ionomer design therefore offers a general strategy for engineering electrochemical interfaces.

title: Predicting Chemical Roles from Database Descriptions Using Natural Language Processing
abstract: In recent years, the use of document information to predict compound activity has gained attention. However, existing methods face challenges in applying these predictions to compounds not included in the training data because of the shortage and insufficient applicability of chemical knowledge as well as in interpreting the basis for predictions. Therefore, this study developed an approach to classifying the chemical roles of these compounds. By analyzing the descriptions of compounds registered in databases using Doc2Vec, we obtained the embeddings.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Efficient simulations of spectra and transport for multiorbital quantum impurities
abstract: Quantum impurity calculations become challenging when multiple correlated orbitals are treated explicitly, particularly in nonequilibrium steady states. We introduce Coupled-Cluster Coupled Lindblad (C$^3$L), a deterministic approach that combines the recently developed coupled-Lindblad compact bath representation with coupled-cluster theory to compute steady states and Green's functions directly in imaginary and real frequency. C$^3$L has favorable polynomial computational complexity and avoids the sign problem of quantum Monte Carlo (QMC). In a real-time multiorbital benchmark, it agrees closely with state-of-the-art QMC while reducing computational cost by four to five orders of magnitude, with a further 10--100-fold speedup on a GPU. Beyond the practical reach of established real-time QMC solvers, four-orbital nonequilibrium impurities with general interactions and biased reservoirs become accessible with C$^3$L. We obtain resonance-resolved transport signatures relevant to scanning tunneling microscopy experiments on molecular junctions.

title: OperAItor: An Agentic Framework for Fault-Tolerant Operation of Chemical Processes
abstract: OperAItor, an open-source framework for developing and evaluating large language model agents for supervisory fault management in chemical processes. The framework is demonstrated on a dynamic reactor-distillation process representing isopropanol dehydrogenation, with physically based thermodynamics and modified reaction kinetics to permit liquid-phase operation. The process is represented by a 113-variable differential-algebraic model and operates at a nominal feed rate of 100kmol/h, producing approximately 4t/h of acetone. The simulated plant includes 8 PI control loops, 22 process alarms, 5 duty-standby pump trains, and 11 independent safety instrumented functions. The agent architecture integrates multivariate statistical process monitoring, fault diagnosis, knowledge-graph retrieval, action planning, and supervisory action generation. Five action-validation configurations are investigated, comprising operation without validation, an LLM-based judge, digital-twin simulation, and deterministic admissibility checks with and without consequence projection. The framework is evaluated using four LLMs across 20 scenarios involving single and multiple simultaneous faults. Without agent intervention, 18 scenarios result in plant stops, corresponding to an economic loss of $399,000 relative to fault-free operation under the assumed benchmark economics. For GPT-5 nano, Qwen3 8B, and Mistral 7B, validated agent configurations reduce the number of stops to 5-8 and recover $265,000 of the loss. The study provides a reproducible benchmark for comparing agent architectures, language models, and action-validation methods for supervisory fault management in chemical processes.

title: Molecular Prior Networks
abstract: Predicting affinity between small molecules and their protein targets remains one of the central problems in drug discovery. Due to the substantial cost of wet-lab experiments, machine learning models of drug-target affinity are usually trained on relatively small datasets, ranging from tens to hundreds of molecules. Given the inherent difficulty of generalization between different targets and chemical series, existing datasets of protein-ligand affinities are typically not used for new projects. At the same time, tabular foundation models, including Prior-data Fitted Networks, have recently shown how transformers can be used to solve machine learning problems in a single forward pass of the network, after being trained over a large corpus of, typically, synthetic datasets. Inspired by that line of work, we propose a novel affinity modelling approach, in which the labels of the query molecules are predicted from the labelled support molecules in a single forward pass of a transformer model. The model is trained on thousands of existing affinity datasets, enabling it to capture the general patterns of molecular activity across different targets, chemical series and dataset sizes. For the smallest support sets, our model matches the state of the art on the regression variant of the FS-Mol benchmark, while being faster than existing methods, thanks to the lack of task-specific training. A comparison against a reduced variant of our architecture, which amounts to kernel regression in a meta-learned feature space, shows that the predictive performance of the transformer model is only partially explained by simple molecular similarity.

title: Harnessing Asymmetric Electrode Dissolution for Highly Reversible Fluorination of Trivalent Metals to Enable Long-Life F-Ion Batteries
abstract: Fluoride-ion batteries (FIBs), owing to high theoretical energy density, are regarded as a key developmental direction for next-generation energy storage systems. However, during cycling, FIBs suffer from the dissolution loss of active materials and the formation of electron–ion insulated fluorination products, which severely hinders interfacial reaction kinetics and cycle stability.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: A novel 5-HT2A receptor-linked signalling pathway involving NAADP-mediated lysosomal Ca2+ release
abstract: Currently there is major research interest in the therapeutic potential of serotonergic psychedelic drugs across a range of neuropsychiatric disorders1-3. Such drugs exert psychedelic and neuroplastic effects, both likely linked to therapeutic outcomes, via agonist action at the 5-HT2A receptor4-7. This receptor is assumed to generate downstream intracellular signalling via an interaction with either Gq protein coupling and formation of the second messenger inositol trisphosphate (IP3), or through triggering the effector {beta}-arrestin2. Central to the IP3 pathway is mobilisation of Ca2+ stored in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). Here, we report the unexpected discovery that the 5-HT2A receptor also signals via an additional second messenger, nicotinic acid adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NAADP), which mobilises Ca2+ release from lysosomal stores. This effect was revealed through measurement of changes in cellular NAADP levels, pharmacological inhibition of NAADP and direct biosensor measurement of lysosomal Ca2+ release and was produced not only by 5-HT but also by a range of psychedelic drugs in a receptor-specific manner. Moreover, genetic ablation of the NAADP pathway reduced markers of both hallucinogenic and neuroplastic effects of psychedelic drug administration in mouse models. These findings reveal the involvement of a novel, therapeutically relevant signalling pathway in psychedelic drug action.

title: More power, less payoff: Study reveals a bottleneck in cleaner methanol production
abstract: Dialing up the power on electricity-driven chemical reactions doesn't guarantee that they'll be more efficient, suggests a new study, a finding that gets researchers closer to creating the ideal conditions for sustainable chemical manufacturing.

title: Multi-Objective Generative Optimization via Expected Hypervolume Fine-Tuning
abstract: Scientific discovery requires plausible designs spanning useful trade-offs among competing properties: a molecule with strong binding affinity, for example, may be difficult to synthesize. Pretrained generative models, e.g., flow and diffusion generators, provide a foundation for proposing such designs, but steering them toward high-quality, complementary trade-offs remains challenging. Inference-time search incurs high per-sample costs, while fine-tuning typically relies on fixed per-candidate rewards that do not capture how designs complement one another. We introduce Hypervolume Fine-Tuning (HVFT), which adapts a single pretrained generator to maximize the expected hypervolume of its samples while controlling departure from the pretrained distribution. Expected hypervolume jointly rewards candidate quality and collective trade-off coverage. Nonetheless, we show that it cannot be expressed as the expectation of a fixed per-candidate reward and therefore cannot be optimized directly with standard techniques. A key observation of this work is that its first variation corresponds to the expected marginal hypervolume contribution of a candidate, which yields a tractable adaptive reward via an unbiased estimator based on model samples. HVFT uses this reward to decompose the objective into a sequence of KL-proximal scalar-reward subproblems. We establish concavity, relative smoothness, and convergence guarantees for the resulting distributional procedure. Across therapeutic-peptide and molecular design tasks spanning discrete diffusion and continuous flow-matching models, HVFT achieves state-of-the-art expected hypervolume and trade-off coverage.

title: Empirical Bayes Flow Matching for Continuous Cryo-EM Heterogeneity
abstract: We address the problem of learning generative priors over high-dimensional latent variables from indirect, noisy observations, with a focus on continuous heterogeneity in cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM). In this setting, 3D atomic structures $x \in \mathbb{R}^{3N_a}$ are never directly observed and must be inferred from 2D projection images $y$ generated by a complex, non-linear forward operator. We propose Empirical Bayes Flow Matching (EB-FM), a method that learns a flow matching prior $p_θ(x)$ directly from observations using a Monte Carlo stochastic approximation Expectation-Maximization framework. EB-FM alternates between an E-step that performs approximate posterior sampling from $p_θ(x \mid y)$ via guided flow-based generation while maintaining persistent latent estimates through stochastic approximation, and an M-step that updates the flow model using these stabilized latent variables as training targets. This approach eliminates the need for pretraining on clean data and naturally accommodates non-linear forward models. We validate our method on controlled inverse problems using two-moons and MNIST data, and demonstrate its effectiveness on simulated cryo-EM data with known poses, showing that EB-FM can recover continuous distributions of protein conformations directly in atomic-coordinate space.

title: iGC: Antibody Optimization via Reinforcement Learning over a Learned Somatic Hypermutation Prior
abstract: Antibody affinity maturation is a natural optimization process in which B cells acquire mutations through somatic hypermutation (SHM), undergo selection for improved antigen binding, and iteratively evolve toward higher affinity. Computationally modeling this process requires capturing both biologically plausible mutations and antigen-specific selection. However, existing mutation models do not directly optimize binding, while affinity optimization often neglects realistic mutation trajectories. We introduce iGC (in silico Germinal Centers), a two-stage reinforcement learning (RL) framework for antigen-specific antibody optimization. Stage 1 learns an SHM mutation prior from parent-child pairs in B-cell lineage trees and adapts it to a target affinity-maturation dataset. Stage 2 initializes an RL policy from this prior and optimizes antigen binding with Kullback-Leibler (KL) regularization toward the frozen prior. To prevent reward exploitation, including repetitive high-reward substitutions and structurally tolerated framework mutations, we introduce a Reward-Tax Meta-Gradient objective. RewardNet smooths the affinity landscape, while TaxNet penalizes reward overexploitation, jointly defining a learned meta-reward for policy optimization. We evaluate iGC on mutation prediction, SHM consistency, affinity optimization, and mutation diversity. The mutation prior more than doubles the strongest baseline in mutation-site prediction.
